Sports.title: Alonso says F1 has ‘very low quality drivers’ at back of grid after Albon collision | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso believes Aston Martin failed to score points despite their strongest showing this year because of his first-lap collision with Alexander Albon.

The pair made contact when Albon tried to pass Alonso on the inside of turn 11. The clash damaged Alonso’s car and he finished the race 16th, four places lower than he started.

“Albon forgot that corner 11 was there and he had to turn left,” said Alonso after the race. “But we need to get better and start a little bit higher up because I think the bottom third of the grid, the quality of the drivers is very low at the moment.”

The stewards did not investigate the collision between the pair.

The two-times world champion believes he could have finished as high as ninth place without the damage he picked up on the first lap.

“I think it was the best race of the year by far for us in terms of competitiveness,” he said. “The car was very strong in the race good tyre management.

“We got a lot of damage on lap one with Albon incident, despite that the car was still competitive. So I think we today we could have had maybe a P9, P10 on merit.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“So the best and the strongest race of the year, but ruined in the first lap with the turn 11 incident.”

Albon said he wasn’t sure if Alonso had noticed him trying to pass on the inside. “I need to review it,” he said, “but I just thought it was lap one, I felt like there was a car on his right side at the time – maybe I’m wrong, I need to have a look.

“But I was on the inside for most of the corner and then it eventually tightened up as it always does in that corner. I tried to get out the way, I was completely on the on the inside kerb. There was a point when I realised he didn’t see me or he was pinched by the car on his right-hand side. I’m sure he got damage, I got damage, so not ideal.

“But we had a second fight. I enjoyed that one a little bit more. I thought that was quite fun, but maybe he doesn’t agree, I’m sure.”

Sports.title: Hadjar urges Red Bull to redesign clutch after another poor start | Formula 1
Sports.content:
A frustrated Isack Hadjar blamed Red Bull’s clutch design for his poor start in the United States Grand Prix.

Hadjar fell from third place to fifth at the start of the race. He went on to finish sixth.

“The clutch needs a redesign because at the moment it’s too fragile, it’s not coping well with temperatures,” he told Sky. “It is a real struggle.”

“I do everything perfect in terms of procedure and then I just have clutch over-delivery,” he added. “These things that are just out of my control, it’s starting to piss me off.”

However Hadjar said the clutch wasn’t the only problem he had to cope with. He complained about the team’s decision to switch him to the hard tyre compound for his second stint.

“I have poor radio coverage, I can’t hear what’s happening like in the pits,” he said. “Then I leave the pits with the wrong [throttle] map and then I’m losing a second a lap every lap on that hard tyre.”

Hadjar’s team mate Max Verstappen, who finished third, also had a list of problems after his race, including a poor start.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It was just the same always in the start, the problem that we have,” he said. “But then the pace is just probably not where we wanted it to be.

“Also I think, for whatever reason, the softer compounds this weekend didn’t really seem to work that well in the race for the first time in a long time. So we were just on the wrong tyres.

“Also I think the way that we used the tyres in the races was the wrong way around, so very quickly it gave away that we had to do a two-stop.

“Then the whole weekend already the power unit has not been consistent, so lap after lap, corner after corner, I’m having different kinds of problems with my engine braking or shifts as well, so I cannot be consistent. That makes it of course very difficult.”

But having won the two grands prix prior to this weekend, Verstappen does not think his car was quick enough to take three in a row.

“Even if we would have done the tyres in the right order or chosen the right compounds, I don’t think we had the pace of Kimi [Antonelli],” he said, “but maybe we could have been second.”

Sports.title: Bearman disagrees with penalty for Gasly collision: ‘I don’t regret going for it’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oliver Bearman disputed the stewards’ decision to penalise him for his collision with Pierre Gasly during the United States Grand Prix.

The pair made contact as Bearman tried to pass Gasly for 10th place. The incident left him with damage which led Haas to retire his car after Bearman served his 10-second time penalty.

“After the [Virtual Safety Car] I managed to get a good launch and [had] good battery level,” Bearman explained. “I caught the two in front of me very quickly and managed to make the Pierre go defensive into turn 12 and then into 13 I sent one up the inside.

“To be honest, yeah I went up his inside, he saw me because he left space, but for me it didn’t really feel like enough. It was a bit of space but only half a car and by the time I was committed, I wasn’t disappearing. So we made a bit of contact.

“I picked up a huge amount of damage on my car. I probably damaged Pierre’s car as well. It was a shame because I felt like I was massively penalised for it anyway. It actually ruined my race, to have that amount of damaged. I was losing a second a lap due to downforce.

“Then on top of that, I picked up a penalty. In my view, it was a racing incident. I sent a move, okay, but I felt like I was entitled to a bit more space than I got. I didn’t lose control. I had to even climb up onto the kerb to try and avoid contact, because I didn’t feel like I was given enough space. So one of those things. The main thing was that I picked up a heck of a lot of damage, and the car was terrible after that, so it was a shame.”

The stewards ruled Bearman was not close enough to Gasly to be entitled to space. “The front axle of car 87 [Bearman] was not ahead of the mirror of car 10 [Gasly] at the apex where a collision occurred

between the two cars,” they noted.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The stewards determined that the driver of Car 87 was wholly to blame for the collision and imposed a 10-second penalty accordingly.”

Bearman was surprised to learn of his penalty, replying “you’re kidding me?” when told on his radio.

Gasly went on to finish in 10th place. Bearman said “I don’t regret going for the move” despite the penalty and damage. “At this stage if we don’t do something special and get a bit lucky and be aggressive and go for it, then we’re not going to score points because we’re fast enough to do that on merit.

“Looking where he is now, I’m happy that he’s likely going to score points after the contact that we had, but I feel like that could have been me and of course that was what I was going for.”

Sports.title: Vasily Lomachenko Targets Charly Suarez for Ring Return at 130.
Sports.content:
Vasiliy Lomachenko is eyeing Charly Suarez for his return at super featherweight, yet defeating the Filipino contender will not settle the core mystery surrounding his comeback: How much elite ability remains after a prolonged absence at age 38?

Suarez is under consideration for his ring return. Lomachenko intends to test his reflexes under real fire prior to chasing premier targets.

“My next step, it will be a fight with a guy, maybe with a guy from the Philippines, Suarez,” Lomachenko said to Fight Hub TV. “It will be my first fight after rest, and after that, we’ll see how I feel.”

Lomachenko has remained inactive since halting George Kambosos Jr. in May 2024. He has not stepped inside the ropes at 130 pounds since 2017, introducing another variable after more than two years on the shelf.

Sharing the ring with Suarez guarantees rounds against an established contender, though any verdict requires scrutiny. Suarez is also 38 years old. Outpointing him offers limited insight into how Lomachenko handles younger, sharper champions across a full championship distance.

Lomachenko built his legendary status on dazzling footwork, spatial control, and split-second precision. He famously pivoted into blind spots, unloading clean punches before opponents could reset. If his reflexes have eroded or his legs can no longer maintain that tempo, fighters who once swung at air might suddenly connect with ease.

Taking on someone like O’Shaquie Foster represents a far steeper hazard. Foster’s slick mobility and sharp counterpunches would force Lomachenko to spend considerable energy establishing range. Looking sharp against Suarez is positive, yet it does not guarantee Lomachenko can cut the ring on Foster or match his pace over 36 minutes.

Lomachenko clearly recognizes the reality in front of him. When questioned regarding matchups with Gervonta Davis or Naoya Inoue, he urged the interviewer to pump the brakes.

“I want to do slowly, slowly, slowly,” Lomachenko noted. “I need to check my body in the real fight.”

Hitting 130 pounds again presents its own physical hurdle. After spending several years up at lightweight, dropping back to a weight class he exited almost ten years ago takes a heavier toll on an older fighter. How comfortably he makes the scale could tell us just as much as his performance under the lights.

The veteran southpaw admitted the ticking clock motivated him to lace up the gloves again instead of letting time slip away.

“One day I wake up and thinking, hey, now I’m 38 years old, and we need to try one more time,” Lomachenko said. “If it will be after two more or three years, then I will be 40, 41 years old. It will be too late.”

His team is scheduled to sit down with Bob Arum to map out the business side of the ring return. Neither a date nor an opponent has been made official.

Suarez offers a workable starting point, though Lomachenko must deliver more than just a victory to prove he still belongs among the division elite. Hand speed, foot mobility, and gas tank over the championship stretch will tell the real story.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Faces Liam Paro In San Francisco
Sports.content:
Devin Haney’s new DAZN deal is getting a favorable launch: a welterweight unification against Liam Paro in San Francisco, with the Australian traveling to Haney’s home region for the opening fight of that agreement.

Mike Coppinger of The Ring reports that the WBO and IBF titleholders will meet December 19 at Chase Center. The fight has yet to receive an official announcement.

It is a legitimate unification. It also puts Haney in the more comfortable position before either man throws a punch. DAZN gets to introduce its newly signed fighter to a Bay Area audience, while Paro arrives with a belt that could make that investment look better by the end of the night.

Paro’s job is to wreck the launch.

He has done something similar before. In June 2024, he traveled to Puerto Rico and beat Subriel Matias by unanimous decision for the IBF light welterweight title. The champion’s reputation and home support failed to intimidate him.

But using that victory as proof he can beat Haney would overlook the harder comparison. Matias came forward and gave Paro opportunities to land while moving. Haney can force him to become the pursuer, making the Australian create openings rather than wait for an opponent to supply them.

That is where this fight could become frustrating for Paro. Following Haney around the perimeter would allow the American to jab, move and make relatively quiet rounds look like his rounds.

Paro needs to attack the body when Haney moves, work when they get close and avoid letting every clinch become a break from the pressure. He cannot afford to spend the first half studying a target that keeps leaving.

Haney has an obligation here, too. A new broadcast deal and two belts will generate promotion, but they cannot substitute for a performance that makes people want his next fight.

Winning narrowly while limiting the action would collect another title. Taking command against a fellow champion would give DAZN something stronger to sell.

The homecoming is arranged around Haney. Whether the night belongs to him depends on how much fighting Paro forces him to do.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Rematch Is The Only Move That Makes Sense For Dalton Smith
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith kept his WBC light welterweight strap in Sheffield, but his reputation took a beating against Alberto Puello.

Eddie Hearn is already talking up a stadium blockbuster against Shakur Stevenson. That talk conveniently skips past the reality left inside the ring: Smith did not convince viewers he solved the man in front of him.

Domestic rival Adam Azim quickly called out the verdict, backing fans who saw the split decision as generous. Two judges handed Smith 115-113 cards, while the third had Puello cruising 116-112.

“Puello won by one round, in my opinion,” Azim told RS Boxing TV, pointing directly to Smith’s lack of urgency.

The deeper issue was how Smith faded down the stretch. Once Puello timed him, Smith went into a shell. His output cratered because every attack opened him up to clean counters.

Instead of building on early rounds, Smith spent the championship rounds fighting in a safety-first manner. He was getting outboxed right when a champion needs to close the show.

Normally, that kind of performance demands an immediate rematch. Matchroom is instead trying to fast-track Smith straight into a massive event with Shakur. The commercial angle makes sense while Smith still holds the belt, but a stadium fight cannot answer the tactical problems Puello exposed.

If Puello made Smith freeze, Shakur’s precision and defensive discipline would make every mistake punishing. Saturday showed zero evidence Smith is ready for that jump. Winning a controversial decision was not the performance Smith needed for Hearn to campaign for a fight with Shakur.

A rematch with Puello is the fight that makes sense. It offers Smith a chance to adjust, keep his work rate up, and earn an undisputed result.

Hearn can sell the official victory, but the ring tells the truth. The belt stayed in Sheffield, while the performance wrecked the case for throwing Smith in with Shakur.

Sports.title: Hearn Bets On A 49-Year-Old Floyd To Strip Ryan Garcia Of His Belt
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn picking Floyd Mayweather to defeat Ryan Garcia says far more about Garcia than Mayweather. A world titleholder at 147 pounds should never be vulnerable against a retiree closing in on 50, yet Hearn genuinely envisions Mayweather stepping off the couch to capture the strap.

“I think Floyd can beat Ryan Garcia. Maybe he’s just too old and maybe he can’t,” said Hearn last Saturday night at a press conference.

The logic assumes Floyd’s timing and defensive muscle memory can outsmart Ryan’s hand speed, even while Floyd’s reflexes and legs are knocking on fifty. That is Hearn basically declaring Ryan has no depth to his game beyond a fast left hook.

Hearn tried legitimizing the spectacle by calling it “almost like a welterweight George Foreman coming back.”

That parallel flatters the concept far too much. Foreman spent years rebuilding, stacking contenders and proving his durability before regaining heavyweight gold. A Mayweather return relies purely on nostalgia, cashing in on past greatness rather than recent proof.

The real problem is the financing of the Mayweather-Garcia fight. Domestic US promoters and traditional networks like DAZN or Amazon Prime Video cannot realistically underwrite this on pay-per-view receipts alone.

Mayweather will demand a guaranteed nine figures, and Garcia will want tens of millions. Traditional pay-per-view models are fractured, and no domestic promoter can guarantee a $150 million purse pot without bleeding cash.

The only entities capable of financing a spectacle of this scale are deep-pocketed sovereign wealth funds or a global streaming giant treating it as a loss leader. If Riyadh Season or a streaming player like Netflix decides the cultural noise is worth lighting tens of millions on fire, the checks clear overnight.

Outside of foreign state funding or a massive corporate subscription grab, traditional American boxing economics simply cannot absorb the guarantees.

Interestingly, Ryan doesn’t seem to care about the social media criticism he’s getting for pursuing a Mayweather fight. As long as millions of people tune in to complain about it, the negative perception simply feeds his bottom line.

If he knocks out an aging Mayweather, he takes credit for ending the most famous undefeated record in modern boxing history. If he loses, he lost to the consensus greatest fighter of this generation.

Sports.title: Canelo Arrives in Riyadh for Mbilli Fight: Start Time, Ring Walks and DAZN PPV
Sports.content:
Canelo returns on October 31 to challenge for the WBC super middleweight belt, live on DAZN PPV and included with DAZN Ultimate.

Canelo Alvarez arrived in Riyadh on Monday morning ahead of his October 31 fight against WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli. The Mexican challenges for a belt he previously held when they meet over 12 rounds at The Venue in Riyadh.

Mbilli had already reached Saudi Arabia. Canelo was welcomed by Faisal Bafarat, chief executive of the General Entertainment Authority, with Jaime Munguia and Rafael Espinoza among the fighters arriving alongside him.

Saturday ends Canelo’s 13-month absence from the ring. The 36-year-old has not fought since Terence Crawford outpointed him in September 2025, stripping him of his undisputed super middleweight championship.

Canelo enters at 63-3-2 with 39 knockouts, seeking to regain a title at 168 pounds. He has won championships in four divisions and twice collected all four major belts at super middleweight.

Mbilli makes his first defence of the full WBC title. The Cameroon-born, Montreal-based champion holds a 29-0-1 record with 24 knockouts, having stopped Maciej Sulecki in the opening round to capture the interim belt in June 2025.

His last fight ended in a split draw against Lester Martinez. He now faces Canelo with his championship and clean loss column at stake.

Canelo vs Mbilli Start Time and Ring Walks

The advertised running order lists preliminary coverage from 10:15 a.m. ET / 7:15 a.m. PT / 2:15 p.m. GMT on Saturday, October 31.

The PPV card begins at 2 p.m. ET / 11 a.m. PT / 6 p.m. GMT.

Canelo and Mbilli’s ring walks are listed for approximately 6 p.m. ET / 3 p.m. PT / 10 p.m. GMT, followed by the opening bell around 6:15 p.m. ET / 3:15 p.m. PT / 10:15 p.m. GMT.

The main event will not begin before 6 p.m. ET / 10 p.m. GMT under that timetable. Individual fight times remain estimates, particularly following changes to the undercard.

How to Watch on DAZN

DAZN PPV costs $79.99 in the United States. The event is also included with DAZN Ultimate, allowing subscribers to that tier to watch without a separate PPV purchase.

Undercard Changes Ahead of Saturday

Jaime Munguia faces Nikita Zon in a scheduled 12-round WBA super middleweight title bout. Their advertised slot is 5 p.m. ET / 9 p.m. GMT.

Rafael Espinoza now faces Ricardo Blandon, replacing Lorenzo Parra for the WBO featherweight title fight. The WBO approved Blandon as the substitute challenger; Espinoza’s original slot was 4 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. GMT.

Raymundo Rojas Garcia meets Reito Tsutsumi over 10 rounds at super featherweight, listed to open the PPV portion at 2 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. GMT.

Lindolfo Delgado’s planned IBF super lightweight title fight against Arthur Biyarslanov is off the card, according to reporter Lance Pugmire. Its previously advertised 2:55 p.m. ET slot should therefore no longer be treated as a confirmed bout time.

Sports.title: Hearn And Warren Let The Wolf In, Says Lou DiBella
Sports.content:
Lou DiBella isn’t buying the victory lap from boxing’s old guard over Zuffa’s early struggles, pointing out that rival promoters helped clear the path for TKO to muscle into the sport to begin with.

Shakur Stevenson walking out the door gave rival outfits an easy talking point, but grabbing free publicity does not suddenly balance a promotion’s checkbook, pack an arena, or supply the massive purse Stevenson expects.

DiBella cut through the noise to ask what these traditional promotional companies are actually gaining from the chaos.

“Is Eddie all of a sudden thriving? Does he have no worries? Is Oscar and Golden Boy great? Is Top Rank’s business getting better? Is anything changing?” said DiBella to Total Boxing.

Taking a victory lap looks hollow when signing an elite free agent immediately turns into a costly headache. Any promoter chasing Stevenson must still lock in an opponent, secure a broadcast budget, and generate enough public interest to justify the deal. Cheering because a fighter hits the open market costs nothing; financing his next outing is another matter entirely.

DiBella also turned the spotlight directly onto Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren for ushering Saudi influence into boxing.

“Who’s most responsible for letting the wolf into the hen house of boxing promotion? It’s Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren.”

Relying on external money delivered massive blockbusters, yet it built an independent power structure capable of pursuing fighters and television rights without needing the old establishment. Whining about an aggressive rival rings hollow after rolling out the red carpet for them.

Even as Zuffa hits growing pains, DiBella believes TKO still holds an edge in sheer muscle, deep political ties, and premier North American broadcast real estate.

“They still have better political and business connections. They still have the best TV deals in North America.”

Those advantages might not guarantee creative matchmaking or commercial success on their own, but deep pockets and broadcast reach give an enterprise plenty of room to absorb early stumbles.

DiBella admitted that everyone inside the sport shares blame for its fragmented condition. Still, his message lands with a thud: taking cheap shots at Dana White brings easy attention, but building a sustainable, busy boxing calendar takes real execution that no competitor can manufacture off another brand’s bad headlines.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Preps For Riyadh As Bektemir Melikuziev Gets Screwed
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia is getting ready to fight Nikita Zon in Riyadh on October 31, but Bektemir Melikuziev is still stuck waiting for the WBA to enforce its own rules. Melikuziev reportedly turned down step-aside cash because he wanted his deserved shot at the belt. Now he risks getting hit with the exact delay he refused to take a check for.

That issue sits right behind the latest training clips floating out of Box Azteca. Munguia is wrapping his hands alongside trainer Eddy Reynoso, grinding through camp while his return date gets closer by the minute. Meanwhile, his number one challenger doesn’t have a clue when his title shot is coming.

The sanctioning body ordered Munguia to face Melikuziev back on September 21, giving both camps until October 21 to strike a deal. Officials pointed out that the mandatory defense window expired on August 30. Once the Zon fight was announced, the WBA posted that it hadn’t approved the bout at all.

It confirmed Melikuziev as the top contender, promising a full review. Yet here we are in late October, with zero public rulings to approve the Riyadh bout, strip the belt, or call a purse bid.

Turning down money to step aside ought to mean something. Melikuziev made it clear he wants the real prize. Letting Munguia cruise ahead without strict conditions gives the champion a pass, leaving the challenger frozen out with nothing to show for standing his ground.

Taking other fights creates real ripple effects. Zon could cause an unexpected cut, a prolonged recovery window, or fresh excuses to stall Melikuziev even longer. Detours like this show that loose promises about future title shots don’t protect anyone.

Missing the October 21 deadline didn’t trigger an automatic stripping, but the original order laid out a purse bid if negotiations crashed. The sanctioning body has a clear procedure ready to go. Leaving fight fans to watch Munguia prep for an unapproved opponent without a formal ruling looks terrible. The WBA needs to order that purse bid right now, or it tells every hungry contender that earning mandatory status means nothing when the champion wants to take a detour.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora’s Inside Game Covers Poor Distance Control
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora’s towering stature is frequently billed as a nightmare puzzle for Jaron “Boots” Ennis. His gritty scrap against Ermal Hadribeaj exposed a deeper issue: height means little if you lack the hand speed and sharp timing to protect it.

Shawn Porter zeroed in on those deficiencies while breaking down Fundora’s October 17 win alongside Hadribeaj. The unheralded challenger slipped past the WBC junior middleweight champion’s reach all night, causing chaos until Fundora finally halted him with one tick remaining in round 12.

“He couldn’t time you last night,” Porter told Hadribeaj Porter’s channel. “You were coming after him, and there was not one moment where he saw you coming.”

Porter mentioned Timothy Bradley’s note that Fundora’s father deliberately schooled him in phone-booth infighting, knowing shorter foes would inevitably crowd him. Preparing for the trenches makes tactical sense. It does nothing to develop range control or a punishing perimeter game.

“You don’t have natural speed with the jab. You don’t have natural timing with the one-two,” Porter pointed out.

That gap undermines Fundora’s physical gifts. An 80-inch reach should turn the outside into a minefield, yet Hadribeaj walked into chest range round after round.

Labeling Fundora an inside specialist lets him off the hook. Smothering a foe by choice after dictating terms from the outside is one thing. Living on the inside because you lack the tools to keep opponents off your chest is entirely different. Porter’s critique puts Fundora squarely in that second camp.

Hadribeaj also smothered Fundora so effectively that the champion lost leverage on his trademark uppercuts. Porter observed that while a few broke through, the challenger took away the arc and velocity that crushed earlier rivals.

That pattern should set off alarm bells for Fundora’s camp ahead of a clash with Ennis.

Hadribeaj was an overlooked mandatory, not a pound-for-pound technician, yet he repeatedly forced the champion into disorganized exchanges.

Ennis would not have to wage a simple war of attrition. Boots could exploit those same entry lanes with explosive combinations, fluid stance switches, and evasive angles before Fundora resets his feet. Breaching Fundora’s perimeter would simply trigger a much heavier assault.

Hadribeaj maintains that Fundora’s rare height might still trouble Ennis. His own 12 rounds offered the opposite verdict: a modest puncher penetrated Fundora’s defenses at will.

Boots would still have to respect the champion’s durability, heavy inside clubs, and unrelenting output. Fundora eventually broke Hadribeaj through pure grit, and absorbing that type of heat drains any gas tank.

Fundora cannot gamble on elite punchers gassing out before his defensive gaps catch up to him. Halting Hadribeaj protected his belt, but it never answered Porter’s questions about how effortlessly he was reached.

Ghana News.title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack
Ghana News.content:
Chris Brown has had hits with tracks like Freaky Friday and Turn Up the Music

US singer Chris Brown has avoided jail after striking a man twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle in a London nightclub.

The R&B star was given an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, over the attack at private members' club Tape in Mayfair, in the early hours of 19 February 2023.

Brown's vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who joined the attack, was sentenced to four months' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months. Both men, who had pleaded guilty to affray, were also ordered to pay £1,500 in costs.

Judge Tony Baumgartner said Brown's use of the glass bottle to hit the victim twice over the head "was plainly dangerous", adding that the violence of the attack was "intense".

The sentence means Brown will not be imprisoned unless he commits another offence during the 12-month period of suspension.

The court heard Brown's attack on music producer Abraham 'Abe' Diaw left the victim in need of hospital treatment for his injuries.

In sentencing, Judge Baumgartner said: "The repeated use of a glass bottle in that way, especially aimed at the head, was plainly dangerous, it carried the risk of delivering a more serious injury than was ultimately sustained."

CCTV footage was shown where Brown struck Diaw four times with the bottle, connecting twice with his head, and then hitting his shoulder.

Sentencing Brown, Judge Baumgartner said: "This was not planned violence. It was nevertheless serious violence by two people in a crowded nightclub."

Chris Brown (left) and Omololu Akinlolu were sentenced at Southwark Crown Court on Monday

The judge told Brown: "Violence of this kind in a crowded nightclub is serious, it creates an obvious risk, not only to the person against whom it is directed, but also to others nearby."

He added that Brown's conduct was "particularly dangerous" and that he had to be "physically pulled away" from the attack.

The judge said Brown's fame, commercial success and professional standing "do not entitle you to special treatment - the law applies equally to everyone".

But judge Baumgartner also said he had noted Brown's guilty plea, compliance with bail conditions, and the impact a custodial sentence would have on Brown's children, and said the singer's "risk of further offending is low".

Brown and Akinlolu pleaded guilty to a charge of affray at Southwark Crown Court in July.

The singer was due to face a trial on more serious charges, which he denied and which were later dropped.

These were assault, attempting to cause grievous bodily harm, and having an offensive weapon.

Following Brown and Akinlolu's guilty pleas, the CPS released a statement outlining that Brown had approached Diaw on the dance floor, hitting him over the head with a glass bottle twice, before Akinlolu then punched Diaw in the head.

"They continued their assault whilst the victim attempted to flee through the club," the CPS said. "The victim was kicked while he was seated defenceless on the floor."

Judge Baumgartner told the pair that while he had concluded they had both crossed the threshold for jail, this year's changes to sentencing laws meant he had to put off doing so unless there were exceptional reasons.

"I have considered whether the seriousness of the offending, taken together with the need for punishment and deterrence, amounts to exceptional circumstances requiring immediate imprisonment. I have concluded, in relation to each of you, that it does not," he said.

"These were serious offences deserving of custodial sentences, but the circumstances do not justify displacing the [new legal] requirement that those sentences be suspended."

Brown's vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, also previously pleaded guilty to affray

On Monday, the court was shown three pieces of CCTV footage from inside Tape nightclub on the night of the attack.

The attack lasted no more than 20 seconds, but Brown could be seen hitting the victim four times with a tequila bottle, twice to the head.

Prosecutor, Heidi Stonecliffe KC, described the weapon as a "heavy square-shaped tequila bottle" and said Diaw was approached by Brown at around 03:00.

The footage showed that the nightclub was very small and packed at the time.

The defence described Chris Brown as a "dedicated and loving father of four children," someone who is "positive and present".

The singer is described as having lived "a good and law-abiding life" since his last conviction in 2013.

The defence described the events at Tape nightclub as a "short and deeply regretted incident".

Brown's defence lawyer told the court that he apologises to all those present at the club at the time of the attack.

"This is an ugly and unattractive incident," Sallie Bennett-Jenkins KC said.

"It is, however, an incident which was very short-lived, lasting something more than 17 seconds but no more than 20.

"It is something which undoubtedly would have caused distress to those who are present and for which Mr Brown... offers a profound apology to all those present."

The court heard Akinlolu "genuinely believed" that Brown was "under attack" when he joined the attack, punching Diaw.

Brown was described as being like a "brother" to Akinlolu, his lawyer Laurie-Anne Power KC told the court.

She added: "He genuinely believed him to be under attack and became involved, and thereafter accepts his initial involvement very quickly evolved into the events he has pleaded guilty to."

Diaw was taken to St Mary's Hospital in London after the attack. Ms Stonecliffe KC said he was discharged with "pain relief and a diagnosis of head injury and superficial injury of the knee".

An MRI scan taken in early March showed a "high grade injury to a ligament on the inner side of the left knee", the court heard.

Defending Brown, Ms Bennett-Jenkins KC said there was a "relatively low level of force" and disputed how significant the injuries were.

The defence argued that the attack left no fractures or broken skin and there was an absence of serious injuries.

Diaw, the victim, was "not supportive of the prosecution" and "withdrew" his support some time after the incident, the court heard.

Chris Brown is one of R&B's most successful singers, with hits including Yeah 3x and Forever

Brown and Akinlolu stood, faced each other, and clasped hands after the judge finished his sentencing remarks before walking out of the glass dock.

Loud cheers rang out outside the court as Chris Brown left the building and appeared to stop to sign an autograph.

After the sentencing, Brown shared a video from inside his car on his Instagram story, showing him looking out the window before turning to the camera and giving a thumbs-up.

Affray is an offence under the Public Order Act, and a person is deemed guilty in law if they use or threaten "unlawful violence towards another" with their behaviour, leading someone to fear for their personal safety.

Brown, 37, is considered one of the biggest stars in R&B, with a string of hit songs including Turn Up The Music, Ayo, Freaky Friday, Run It, Forever, Yeah 3x and Don't Wake Me Up.

Ghana News.title: Ballon d’or 2026: De la Fuente wins 2026 Ballon d’Or Coach of the Year Award after Spain’s World Cup triumph
Ghana News.content:
Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente has been named the 2026 Men’s Coach of the Year at the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, capping a remarkable year in which he led the national team to FIFA World Cup glory.

The 65-year-old claimed the Johan Cruyff Trophy on Monday, October 26, after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final on July 19, securing the country’s second men’s world title.



De la Fuente’s latest achievement adds another major honour to a coaching career that has flourished since he took charge of Spain’s senior national team in December 2022.



His World Cup success has also placed him among the most accomplished coaches in Spanish football, following the country’s victories at the 2023 UEFA Nations League and Euro 2024.



De la Fuente beats coaching heavyweights

The Spanish tactician emerged ahead of an impressive shortlist featuring Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, Paris Saint-Germain’s Luis Enrique, Aston Villa boss Unai Emery and Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany.



The award recognises De la Fuente’s work in guiding Spain through a successful international campaign, culminating in victory over Argentina in a dramatic final that was decided in extra time.



Spain secured the trophy through Ferran Torres’ 106th-minute strike after Argentina had held them goalless during normal time.



The victory also made De la Fuente the oldest coach to win the men’s FIFA World Cup, at 65 years and 28 days, surpassing the previous record held by compatriot Vicente del Bosque, who led Spain to the 2010 title.

Spain’s historic World Cup campaign



Spain’s triumph was built on a disciplined and largely dominant tournament performance.



De la Fuente’s side went unbeaten throughout their eight matches at the expanded 2026 World Cup, conceding just one goal during the competition.



Goalkeeper Unai Simón also recorded seven clean sheets, setting a tournament record for the most shutouts by a goalkeeper in a single men’s World Cup edition.

Spain’s victory over Argentina further strengthened the country’s position among international football’s leading forces, adding the world title to its recent continental and international successes.



The achievement also made Spain the first country to hold the men’s and women’s FIFA World Cup titles simultaneously, following the women’s team’s triumph in 2023.



A new milestone for Spain’s coach



The Johan Cruyff Trophy gives De la Fuente individual recognition for the success he has overseen with Spain, following years of development work within the country’s national-team system.

Before taking charge of the senior side, he worked with Spain’s youth teams, helping develop players who have since become central to the national team’s success.



His senior-team achievements include the 2023 Nations League, Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup, a run of major honours that has established his reputation among Europe’s leading international coaches.



The 2026 award also places a national-team manager at the top of a category whose previous winners came from the club game, marking a significant moment for international coaching.



For De la Fuente, the recognition completes an extraordinary year in which Spain returned to the summit of world football and his work on the touchline earned one of the sport’s most prestigious individual coaching honours.

Ghana News.title: Pennant has more than 50 stitches after dog attack
Ghana News.content:
Former Premier League footballer Jermaine Pennant says he needed more than 50 stitches after being mauled by a dog.

The 43-year-old was walking his two dogs in north London last week when he was attacked by a German Shepherd.

The former Liverpool and Stoke City winger said the dog latched on to his leg and refused to let go as he tried to protect his own dog, King.

King then intervened to help fight off the attacking dog, preventing "what could've been a horrendous situation", Pennant said in a post on Instagram.,

Pennant told the Sun he required more than 50 stitches to his right leg after sustaining four bite wounds in the attack and receiving hospital treatment.

He added that King was unhurt, but did not give details about the German Shepherd. He said he declined to report the attack to police.

"So I was attacked by a German Shepherd. I tried to protect King, but the dog got my leg. I was on the floor with the dog still attached, with no sign of letting go, until King intervened, as he didn't know what was going on," said Pennant.

"But the minute he did, he fought the dog off and saved what could've been a horrendous situation for me.

"King was unhurt, with a little nip on his leg, but had blood all over him which wasn't mine. At this point I forgot the agony I was in, and my heart sank, but it wasn't King's."

The picture uploaded to Instagram shows Pennant with a bandage on his leg alongside King on a sofa, while he also thanked his partner, Mimmi Montgomery, for looking after them.

"My hero still protecting me and trying to look after me. King, you're a legend, love you, man's best friend. Thanks, Mimmi Montgomery, for taking care of us both."

Pennant, a Talksport pundit, made 231 Premier League appearances in a 19-year career before retiring in 2018.

At 15, before his professional debut, Pennant became the most expensive trainee in English football when he joined Arsenal from Notts County for £2.5m.

Ghana News.title: Ballon d’or 2026: Lamine Yamal makes history with third straight Kopa Trophy win
Ghana News.content:
Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal has made football history after winning the 2026 Kopa Trophy for the third consecutive year, becoming the first player to claim the award three times.

The 19-year-old Spain international received the honour at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London on Monday, October 26, following another impressive season in which he helped Barcelona win La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup before playing a key role in Spain’s 2026 FIFA World Cup triumph.



Yamal’s latest success extends his dominance in the award, which recognises the best young footballer under the age of 21. He previously won the trophy in 2024 and 2025.



His third consecutive victory puts him ahead of previous winners, including Kylian Mbappé, Matthijs de Ligt, Pedri, Gavi and Jude Bellingham, who have each won the award once.



The Barcelona star beat several highly rated young players to retain the honour, including teammate Pau Cubarsí, Yan Diomande, Lennart Karl, Warren Zaïre-Emery and Johan Manzambi.



Yamal’s achievement comes after a successful 2025-2026 campaign at both club and international levels. He was instrumental in Barcelona’s domestic success and featured prominently in Spain’s run to the World Cup title, which they secured with a 1-0 victory over Argentina in the final.



His performances have continued to strengthen his reputation as one of the most exciting talents in world football, with his dribbling, creativity and attacking influence making him a key figure for both Barcelona and Spain.

Despite his personal achievement, Yamal expressed a preference for his Barcelona teammate Cubarsí to have won the award, according to reports from the ceremony. He praised the defender’s performances while expressing gratitude to his club and national team.



Yamal’s third Kopa Trophy also adds to Barcelona’s impressive record in the award’s history. The club previously produced winners Pedri in 2021 and Gavi in 2022, before Yamal began his consecutive run in 2024.



The 2020 edition was not awarded, while Mbappé won the inaugural prize in 2018, de Ligt claimed it in 2019 and Bellingham was named the winner in 2023.



At 19, Yamal remains eligible for the award in future editions before turning 22, giving him the opportunity to extend his record.



His latest triumph further cements his status among the leading young players in the game, as attention turns to whether he can translate his growing collection of individual honours into further success with Barcelona and Spain.

Ghana News.title: Amelley Djosu: The culture we create, the abuse we excuse and the responsibility of Ghana’s creative industry
Ghana News.content:
The allegations of sexual abuse involving 19 students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School have renewed a difficult conversation about the safety of young people, the abuse of authority and the systems meant to protect them.

The allegations must be investigated thoroughly and treated seriously without prejudging the outcome. Yet the wider questions they raise cannot wait for a verdict. What kind of society are we building when young people may struggle to recognise abuse, report it or trust that someone will protect them?

As a marketing communications strategist, creative entrepreneur and advocate for responsible creative practice, I believe this conversation must extend beyond schools and law enforcement. It must include the media, musicians, filmmakers, comedians, influencers, brands and everyone whose work shapes public attitudes.

Sexual abuse is not caused by music videos, comedy skits or social media trends alone. But the culture we create can either challenge the abuse of power or make it easier to excuse.

When entertainment shapes what society tolerates

Creativity reflects society, but it also influences how society sees itself. Music, film, comedy and digital content shape ideas about relationships, gender, power and acceptable behaviour, particularly among young audiences.

Consider the objectification of women in some music videos, lyrics that reduce them to sexual objects, and scenes that portray unwanted touching or persistent sexual advances as playful or harmless. Add online skits that turn harassment into comedy without questioning the behaviour, and a troubling pattern emerges.

The problem is not that art explores sexuality, attraction or adult relationships. Artistic freedom matters, and provocative content should not automatically be treated as harmful. The concern is what happens when entertainment repeatedly blurs the line between attraction and entitlement, persistence and coercion, or humour and humiliation.

When a woman's refusal becomes a challenge to overcome, or a child's vulnerability becomes entertainment, audiences risk becoming less sensitive to the harm beneath the joke.

Representation does not automatically determine behaviour, and responsibility for abuse rests with the person who commits it. But creatives cannot dismiss their cultural influence simply because their work is entertainment.

The question is not whether creatives are responsible for every social problem. It is whether they are willing to take responsibility for the messages they choose to amplify.

Consent is not a trend, it is a standard.

Consent requires a clear, voluntary agreement. It cannot be inferred from silence, fear, a previous flirtation or a relationship. Nor does a position of authority give anyone the right to exploit another person.

Where children are concerned, the responsibility is even greater. Teachers, coaches, religious leaders and other adults entrusted with their care have a duty to protect, not exploit. No creative narrative should blur the distinction between safeguarding a child and sexualising one.

The Obuasi allegations therefore demand more than public outrage. They require credible investigations, protection for complainants, accountability where wrongdoing is established, and safe channels for reporting misconduct. Institutions must not confuse protecting their reputation with protecting vulnerable people.

The creative industry also has a role. Comedians can challenge harmful behaviour without trivialising abuse. Musicians can create compelling work without reducing women to props. Filmmakers can portray difficult realities without glamourising exploitation. Influencers can use their platforms to make conversations about consent, boundaries and safeguarding more accessible.

Actor and content creator Jeffrey Nortey, for instance, has used skits to address consent, inappropriate advances and the abuse of minors. His work illustrates how comedy can open up difficult conversations without sacrificing entertainment. With thoughtful writing, humour can do more than attract attention. It can challenge audiences to reconsider what they have come to accept.

Responsibility must run through the creative value chain

This responsibility cannot rest on individual artists alone. Producers, directors, scriptwriters, publicists, talent managers, media organisations, advertisers and sponsors all influence what gets made, funded, promoted and celebrated.

Brands should look beyond reach and engagement when choosing creative partners. Popularity matters, but so do professional conduct and judgement. Content that attracts millions of views while normalising harassment may generate attention without building meaningful brand value.

Media organisations, too, must report allegations responsibly. Sensational headlines, unnecessary exposure of complainants and speculative commentary can deepen the harm. Reporting should avoid victim-blaming, protect identities where required and clearly distinguish allegations from established findings.

Practical safeguards are equally important. Production houses and event organisers should establish clear codes of conduct, protect minors, provide safe reporting channels and respond seriously to complaints. Creative organisations can help by developing professional standards and ensuring members are held accountable.

Awareness campaigns alone are not enough. A powerful public message about consent means little if the people delivering it tolerate harassment behind the scenes.

Beyond outrage, towards cultural change

Ghana has no shortage of public condemnation when disturbing allegations emerge. The challenge is turning outrage into lasting change.

Parents and schools must help young people understand boundaries and feel safe speaking up. Authorities must investigate complaints fairly and thoroughly. Institutions must guard against retaliation. The media must report responsibly, and the creative industry must examine what it normalises in the pursuit of views, applause and commercial success.

Blaming music, comedy or popular culture for the actions of abusers would be simplistic and unfair. Sexual abuse involves individual choices, unequal power and failures of accountability. But culture influences how harmful behaviour is interpreted, challenged or excused. Creatives are therefore part of the conversation, not because they are responsible for every harm, but because they have the reach to challenge harmful attitudes and make healthier ones visible.

The measure of a socially conscious creative industry is not how quickly it joins a trending conversation after a scandal. It is whether its work and professional practices help build a culture in which consent is respected, children are protected and abuse is never treated as entertainment.

We cannot expect art to solve every social problem. We can, however, expect those who shape public culture to think carefully about the world their work helps create.

Our creative industry cannot control every individual who abuses power. But it can help change what society tolerates, what it celebrates and what it refuses to excuse.

That responsibility is not a distraction from creativity. It is part of what makes influence worth having.

About the author:

Amelley Djosu is a marketing communications strategist, creative entrepreneur and journalist who writes on the intersections of culture, creativity, commerce and social responsibility. She is interested in how Ghana's creative industry can use its influence to shape public conversations, promote professional standards and contribute to meaningful social change.

Ghana News.title: Kane prematurely announced as Ballon d’Or winner – but he wasn’t only one
Ghana News.content:
For a moment, it seemed as though Harry Kane's dreams of winning the Ballon d'Or had come true.

It was shortly after 17:15 GMT on Monday when an article from the award's official website titled "Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or" began to circulate online.

It was more than four and a half hours before the winner of the game's most prestigious individual award was due to be announced at a star-studded event at London's Palladium Theatre.

The article's widespread sharing caused confusion online, with some wondering whether France Football, the award's organisers, had failed at the final hurdle of keeping the winner, voted by journalists at the end of September, under wraps.

That was until further digging on the Ballon d'Or website revealed that other favourites to win the award, including Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe, had also had similar pieces written and published about them.

When asked about the articles by BBC Sport, a Ballon d'Or spokesperson said: "Some profiles of nominees prepared by BallonDor.com were inadvertently published online.

"These articles had been prepared for all nominees and should in no way be considered as an indication of the final results or rankings"

Just before 17:40 BST, the articles about Kane and Mbappe had been removed from the website.

Similar articles also covered London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas and Barcelona's Ewa Pajor, two of the favourites for the corresponding women's award, also taking place on Monday night.

If Kane is to realise his dream and become the first Englishman to win the award since 2001, he will have to wait a little longer to find out.

Ghana News.title: More than 60 Christians killed in Ethiopia ‘massacre’, church official says
Ghana News.content:
More than 60 people have been killed in a series of attacks on Christians in Ethiopia's Oromia region, according to the country's Orthodox Church.

One resident, whose 75-year-old father was killed, described it as an ambush. "We were completely unprepared and had no prior knowledge. They surrounded us from all four directions," he told BBC Amharic.

The regional government said that it would take action against those responsible.

A local official blamed the attacks on a newly formed rebel coalition, the Alliance for Survival, which includes the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA). The OLA has not commented but has denied carrying out previous such attacks.

A statement from the Holy Synod of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church said that 20 houses were burnt to the ground in the attacks. It did not say who was responsible.

Eyewitness told BBC Amharic that five of those killed were children.

A church official described the attacks on three areas in the Shirka district as a "massacre", saying security forces arrived at the scene but were unable to stop the assault.

Many residents have now fled the area.

Condemning the violence, the Orthodox Church said attacks against Christians had been increasing recently, and that "such actions undermine the country's values of mutual respect and peaceful coexistence".

In a statement posted on Facebook, the Orthodox Church said it had repeatedly raised concerns about insecurity with authorities at different levels of government, but that "so far there has been no solution".

The Ethiopian Human Rights Council, a non-governmental organisation, said in a report released in July 2026 that 458 people had been killed in attacks in that area over the previous four years.

But this is one of the most deadly attacks in that period.

The report said armed groups had repeatedly targeted local communities, particularly followers of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, in what it described as religiously motivated attacks.

The government has previously blamed the OLA for the attacks, with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed saying violence targeting civilians and religious institutions was part of a plan to destabilise the country.

The group, which says it is fighting for greater rights for the Oromo people, denies these allegations.

Previous reports have also documented attacks against Muslims in the area. Residents who spoke to the BBC on various occasions have described the violence as both ethnic and religious in nature.

About two-thirds of Ethiopians are Christians, mostly Orthodox, while one third are Muslim.

Ghana News.title: Seven families to press charges against Obuasi SHTS headmaster amid threats and blackmail
Ghana News.content:
Seven families of girls allegedly sexually abused by the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High and Technical School (SHTS) are preparing to press charges against him, amid reported threats, intimidation and attempts to blackmail those seeking justice.

The decision follows engagements between the families, the victims and officials from the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection during an official visit to Obuasi to support the victims and advance efforts to secure justice.

During the engagement, the affected families and girls recounted their alleged ordeal to the government officials, detailing their experiences.

However, the pursuit of justice is reportedly being complicated by threats against some of the families, with concerns that intimidation is discouraging others from openly participating in the case.

Gender Minister, Dr. Agnes Lartey, disclosed that her ministry is working with National Security to identify and deal with individuals allegedly threatening or blackmailing the victims and their families.

She said authorities were also taking steps to remove audio and video recordings circulating on social media that expose the identities of the girls, particularly content mentioning their full names.

“We are working with National Security to pull down those audios and videos, if possible, the ones that mention their full names so that the families will feel safe and protected,” she said.

The Minister indicated that the process had already commenced but declined to provide further details, citing concerns that the threats were connected to the ongoing efforts to pursue accountability.

“I don’t want to give details because their threats are centred around that, and it is not just political. Threats are coming from families and other influential persons,” she stated.

She added that efforts were underway to trace those allegedly making threatening and blackmailing calls, with the aim of bringing them before the law.

“We are finding a way to track those who are calling to blackmail and threaten them so that we bring them to book as offenders of the law,” she said.

The Minister further revealed that more than seven people have been identified as willing to support the case, although fear of possible repercussions was forcing some to remain behind the scenes.

According to her, at least one person had indicated a willingness to support the legal process privately but was reluctant to appear publicly or formally report the matter because of threats and pressure from family members.

“We are having more than seven people now. One of them felt them it’s beyond him so he said he and the family can support from behind but because of the threats from family. How the issue has escalated overwhelms some of them, so they want to support the case in running but not to show up to report.

“But because of the threats from family, and how the issue has escalated, it overwhelms some of them. They want to support the case in running, but not to show up to report,” she said.

The disclosure highlights the challenges confronting efforts to secure justice for the alleged victims, as concerns over intimidation and exposure continue to weigh on families deciding whether to participate in the case.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: What will Lula’s fourth term mean for Brazil?
World.content:
Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva wins a fourth term as Flavio Bolsonaro disputes the result. Can Lula deliver on his promises of change?

Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva delivered a defiant message after being declared the winner of a run-off vote on Sunday.

He lost round one to his right-wing rival. But he made history by coming out on top in the second poll.

Opponent Flavio Bolsonaro has disputed the result and says he wants it annulled.

This will be Lula’s fourth nonconsecutive term in office. He’s promised a new approach to governing. But many challenges lie ahead. So, how will his government handle them?
