World.title: Iraq, Jordan sign nine memoranda of understanding
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Jordan signed on Monday nine memoranda of understanding and executive programs in Amman.

The agreements were finalized during an official visit by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who met with Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan and King Abdullah II to enhance bilateral ties and economic integration.

The agreements span economic, diplomatic, educational, and cultural sectors, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The agreements include managing competition policies and preventing market monopolies, protecting the ecosystem and biodiversity, a five-year plan to expand university research cooperation and academic partnerships, and mechanisms to safeguard consumer rights and trade standards, as well as collaboration on historical preservation, manuscripts, and national archives.

They also cover a partnership between Iraq’s Foreign Service Institute and Jordan’s Diplomatic Institute, support for small and medium-sized enterprises, an executive program for bilateral cultural exchange, and a multi-year framework establishing core educational sector cooperation.

Al-Zaidi formally proposed establishing a joint free zone to boost commercial volume and position Iraq as a regional economic hub.

The Iraqi prime minister’s trip to Jordan comes ahead of planned visits to Lebanon and Syria.

World.title: Vessel reportedly catches fire off the coast of Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) issued a warning on Monday after receiving multiple third-party reports of a vessel on fire 63 nautical miles (116.6 kilometers) southeast of al-Faw, Iraq.

The UKMTO has officially classified the incident as suspicious activity. The crew’s current status, the exact extent of the damage, and any potential environmental impacts remain unknown.

The warning issued on Monday did not identify the vessel or specify the cause of the fire.

According to UKMTO, vessels transiting the northern Arabian Gulf are advised to exercise extreme caution and report any suspicious activity to authorities.

Attacks and hostile security incidents targeting commercial vessels in the far northern Arabian Gulf near Iraq have surged drastically, turning the waters surrounding Iraq’s primary oil terminals into an active maritime conflict zone.

A few days ago, a tanker’s master claimed being hit by an unidentified missile 30 nautical miles (55.5 kilometers) southeast of al-Faw in a different incident.

World.title: Iraq proposes establishing free zone with Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi emphasized on Monday the importance of establishing a free zone between Iraq and Jordan to bolster trade exchange between the two countries.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place when he and Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan co-chaired an expanded meeting between the Iraqi and Jordanian delegations in the capital, Amman.

The meeting addressed approaches to strengthen bilateral relations in different sectors, particularly energy, the economy, and investment, to serve the mutual interests of both countries, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

As it aims to enhance cooperation in the economic, commercial, industrial, and security sectors, al-Zaidi emphasized the importance of his visit to Jordan.

The meeting addressed regional developments, emphasizing the importance of the Palestinian cause.

In addition to supporting diplomatic efforts to confront obstacles, resolve crises, and lessen their negative impacts at the regional and global levels, it emphasized the significance of securing justice for the Palestinian people and restoring their full rights.

Al-Zaidi underscored Jordan’s role as a strategic partner and expressed Iraq’s eagerness to enhance cooperation with its neighboring country to tackle various challenges and further strengthen bilateral relations.

World.title: Iraqis mark 7th anniversary of 2019 Tishreen Uprising
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Thousands of Iraqis gathered on Sunday in Baghdad’s Tahrir Square and southern provinces to mark the seventh anniversary of the 2019 Tishreen (October) Uprising.

Major centers, including Baghdad, Najaf, Nasiriyah, and Basra saw a resurgence of protests, with activists bringing national and local problems back to the scene.

Activists are still calling for justice and the punishment of those who murdered more than 600 demonstrators during the initial crackdowns in 2019.

Protesters explicitly voiced their opposition to regional external influence, shouting anti-Iranian chants and demanding an end to foreign interference in Iraqi politics.

The muhasasa system, a sectarian political quota system that divides political posts and state resources among controlling parties, is still being opposed by protesters.

Protesters demanded that all weapons be restricted to state authority, targeting the power of Iranian-backed armed militias operating in the country.

Popular infrastructure failure, significant young unemployment, and widespread government corruption continue to be major sources of public frustration.

Iraqi security officials deployed forces to safeguard important squares and public areas ahead of the anniversary, putting soldiers in Baghdad on high alert to prevent possible escalations.

The 2019 Tishreen Uprising was the largest, longest-lasting, and most significant social movement in Iraq’s post-2003 history.

The nonviolent movement, which was mostly spearheaded by frustrated youth, broke out in Baghdad and southern Iraq on October 1, 2019, demanding a complete reform of the country’s political system.

World.title: Man Utd crisis deepens as Carrick faces axe
World.content:
Manchester – Winless in eight games and hovering just above the Premier League relegation zone, struggling Manchester United are facing the prospect of yet another managerial change, with Michael Carrick likely to pay the price.

The former United midfielder was warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel after his team’s chastening 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch — with fans clear in their minds where the blame lies for United’s current malaise.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.

But a drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson.

An emotional Carrick denied his lap of the pitch at full-time on Sunday was a goodbye as he struggles to come to terms with his team’s precipitous decline.

“I definitely knew that we hadn’t cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn’t mean to say that it should have gone this way,” he said.

Carrick, 45, is clinging on but his position appears increasingly precarious, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann apparently in the frame for the job.

The United boss, who won multiple titles in the club’s golden era under Ferguson, was the seventh permanent appointment since the Scot retired.

David Moyes was proven in the Premier League, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho had stellar records and Erik ten Hag and Amorim were seen as rising stars of coaching.

– Sentimental choice –

Carrick is in the same category as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who was in charge for three years from 2018 — a sentimental choice as a former player who played a major role in the club’s glory years under Ferguson.

“The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what’s going to happen here. They’ve seen this before. He’s one of their own and he’s popular,” former United captain Gary Neville told Sky Sports.

“But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular and they’ve badly let this football club down.”

The problems at the club, as Neville points out, go far beyond the dugout.

Despite fierce, ongoing protests from fans, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts.

Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have been dashed.

Ratcliffe has overseen cost-cutting measures including widespread redundancies and ticket hikes but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.47 billion).

United, who for years bullied their rivals in the transfer market, lost out on the biggest names as they targeted a summer midfield rebuild, with Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes all choosing other clubs.

United instead recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos — none of whom have made a strong impression — for combined fees of about £150 million.

Significant rifts have emerged in recent weeks.

Lisandro Martinez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox for not doing more to strengthen Carrick’s squad.

Last week captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 humbling by Champions League debutants Como.

Carrick is expected to take the blame, but the route back to the top for one of the world’s biggest clubs appears tougher than ever.

“It can’t just be the manager again. There has got to be consequences above that. You can’t keep letting the people pick the manager who keep getting it wrong,” said Neville.

“It’s years now without a Premier League title. That will be another five or 10 before you know it because there are other clubs set up for success and Manchester United aren’t.”

World.title: Kane tipped to beat Yamal, Mbappe to Ballon d’Or glory
World.content:
London – Harry Kane is favourite to become England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years when the award is presented in London on Monday, but he faces stiff competition from La Liga pair Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Alexia Putellas is the clear frontrunner to win the women’s prize for a third time, with Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign set to come to an end after an injury-hit spell.

The ceremony to decide the world’s best male and female footballers is being held in London for the first time — 70 years after England winger Stanley Matthews was presented with the inaugural award.

Bayern Munich and England forward Kane struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double.

But semi-final exits in both the Champions League and at the World Cup in the United States mean a triumph for Kane at the London Palladium is far from certain.

“I’d love to be able to achieve something like that. It would be a massive milestone in my career,” said the 33-year-old former Tottenham forward.

“I think my wife would prefer to know and my family… it’s very stressful for everyone,” added the England captain.

Only four players from England have won the Ballon d’Or. Michael Owen was the last to triumph in 2001, following in the footsteps of Matthews, Bobby Charlton and Kevin Keegan.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany praised Kane’s focus on his team, saying: “What made Harry happy the most in recent years is that he finally won his first team trophies here.

“Now if he can crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be deserved for the way he plays for the team.”

– ‘I deserve it’ –

Yamal finished second to Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembele last year and the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar seems destined to be a Ballon d’Or winner one day.

However, a hamstring injury ended his club season early and he failed to show his most irresistable form during Spain’s World Cup triumph, which was built on impressive teamwork.

But that has not diminished his confidence ahead of the ceremony.

“For me, Mbappe and me, we’re the two best players in the world,” Yamal said last month.

“I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I’ve won.”

Mbappe, by contrast, boasts plenty of personal milestones without medals for either Real Madrid or France.

The 27-year-old was top goalscorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup without winning any of those trophies.

His 10 World Cup goals in North America made him the top goalscorer in the competition’s history, on 22.

“Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out,” said Mbappe.

“Who am I voting for? Myself.”

The Ballon d’Or was established by the magazine France Football, with the first award given to Matthews in 1956.

One football journalist from each of the 100 top nations in FIFA’s rankings is invited to cast votes for their top 10 players from a 30-man shortlist.

Although the award carries no cash prize, it can generate huge bonuses from clubs and commercial partners as well as increasing a player’s overall market value.

Putellas, winner of the women’s award in 2021 and 2022, was a member of the Barcelona side that regained the Champions League last season before moving to London City Lionesses.

Her former Barcelona team-mate, Poland’s Ewa Pajor, is Putellas’s main challenger after scoring 11 Champions League goals in Barca’s latest triumph.

World.title: Iraqi PM makes official visit to Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived on Monday in the Jordanian capital, Amman, for his first official visit to the neighboring country since taking office.

King Abdullah II received Al-Zaidi at Amman Civil Airport. Leading a high-level delegation, al-Zaidi’s visit comes in response to an invitation from the Jordanian king.

Amid ongoing tensions, the two leaders are meeting to discuss security concerns in the region, joint development initiatives, and economic cooperation.

The two countries are expected to sign several memoranda of understanding (MoUs) to advance joint economic initiatives.

Al-Zaidi and King Abdullah II are expected to discuss approaches to strengthen bilateral relations, as well as mechanisms for cooperation to address various challenges.

Furthermore, the two leaders will chair an expanded meeting between the delegations of the two countries and oversee the signing of several memoranda of understanding aimed at fostering cooperation, integration, and economic partnership, while safeguarding mutual interests.

The trip reflects a shared vision between Baghdad and Amman to expand regional dialogue and promote solutions that ensure long-term stability across the Middle East.

World.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran
World.content:
Riyadh – Yemen’s Houthis have kept up their attacks on Saudi Arabia as senior officials from the kingdom, Turkey and Pakistan are due to hold high-stakes talks with Iran in Tehran on Monday, following warnings of a return to war.

Fresh explosions rattled Riyadh overnight, along with a text message warning to residents, after the Iran-allied Houthis claimed a new attack on the Saudi capital’s international airport on Sunday.

Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, has become deeply embroiled in the eight-month war since hostilities in its long-running conflict with the Iran-allied Houthis resumed in July.

Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman is among the delegations travelling to Tehran, made up of officials from the three countries that signed a defence alliance in Mecca in August.

Their visit follows warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could resume.

Tensions have increased ahead of Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday and next week’s US mid-terms, where US President Donald Trump’s Republicans are battling to keep control of both chambers of the US Congress.

Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei will take part in Monday’s meeting with Prince Khalid, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Ali Bagheri Kani, told state TV.

“This historic meeting in Tehran may be the last chance before escalation spirals out of control, an attempt to impose a path of de-escalation before it’s too late,” Hesham Alghannam, a Saudi security analyst and researcher, posted on X.

“The presence of military and security figures at this level together means that the remaining time is extremely limited.”

– ‘Serious tensions’ –

On Sunday, as blasts rang out over Riyadh and authorities sent texts warning residents of a “hostile aerial threat”, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it struck missile launchers and storage facilities in Yemen.

The Houthis said they had attacked Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport once again. The repeatedly targeted facility has been largely closed since 13 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in a major attack this month.

Mediation efforts between the US and Iran have been led by Qatar and Pakistan. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Sunday, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said.

“Our region is in the grip of serious tensions, and neighbouring countries are striving to convey a message and put forward initiatives,” Baqaei said on Monday.

Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy MENA analytica said Prince Khalid’s presence in Tehran was “hugely significant”, calling him the “strategic mastermind of Saudi Arabia”.

Prince Khalid, brother of Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has emerged as one of Saudi Arabia’s key diplomatic interlocutors, dispatched on sensitive regional missions.

“For him to go to Iran directly in this very sensitive time is a very, very strong signal that the kingdom is not just… sitting and waiting for things, events to unfold,” Krieg told AFP.

“There’s a clear effort by the Mecca alliance to signal to Iran that they’re ready to work together to defend the kingdom and defend the kingdom’s borders,” he added.

“And so should Iran think to escalate, which they will likely do if Israel and the US strikes, and they will most likely strike Saudi Arabia, Iran will have to bear the consequences.”

– ‘Don’t test us’ –

Comments by senior officials have raised speculation about renewed hostilities.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday “there has been talk of a new war” but that Tehran’s policies remain unchanged.

Trump said on Friday that Washington “may do another little Epic Fury”, referring to the US-Israeli campaign against Iran that began on February 28.

On Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran may try to disrupt the Israeli elections, where he is in a close-fought race to stay in power.

“We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections,” Netanyahu said.

“Don’t test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows,” added Netanyahu, who has campaigned heavily on his security credentials.

The remarks came as Israel’s Channel 12, citing unnamed sources, reported a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied.

World.title: No action on deleted voters using Form 6: Supreme Court
World.content:
New Delhi: No one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter their name in electoral rolls, the

verbally assured electors on Monday. It allayed fears that use of Form 6, which asks applicants to declare they are fresh voters, for re-inclusion in draft electoral rolls could invite prosecution for false declaration.

The statement came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohan while hearing a PIL against large-scale exclusion of names from

âs draft electoral roll and as a response to senior advocate Aravind Datarâs plea that using Form 6 for re-inclusion would amount to lying under oath.

Will grant time to genuine voters to submit papers if out from final list: SC

The bench also said that if it found there were genuine voters whose names could not be included in the final electoral list, to be published on Nov 6, it could grant them more time to submit their documents for the purpose.

A similar concern was raised by advocate Prashant Bhushan 10 days earlier while questioning the ECâs directive that voters whose names were deleted from Delhiâs draft electoral roll during SIR exercise use Form 6 to restore them in draft rolls.

Datar said that with two crore voters excluded from Maharashtraâs draft electoral roll, including 1.22 crore on grounds of logical discrepancy, and the deadline for claims and objections ending on Oct 26, many voters who were removed on flimsy and non-existent grounds would have little chance of getting names restored.





The senior advocate requested the bench to extend the Oct-26 deadline for those seeking inclusion of their names in the electoral roll. The bench asked the EC to file its response to the PIL by Nov 5 and said it would examine on that day whether extra time would be required for those seeking inclusion of names.

Datar said, âIn Maharashtra, 33% of voters have been deleted. In Mumbai, 40% of the voters have been excluded. What is happening is people are asked to fill Form 6, which is meant for fresh voters.

There is no provision for a person who had voted in the last three or four elections to get his name restored in the voter list. If he fills Form 6, which is meant for registration of fresh voters, then he would face prosecution for false declaration.

â

However, the CJI allayed these fears and said, âNo one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voter lists.â Datar said that since there was no imminent election in Maharashtra, the SC could direct EC not to finalise the electoral roll for the state on Nov 6 and postpone the schedule to enable genuine voters to re-enter them in voter lists. The bench also said, âIf we find, even after the publication of the final electoral roll, that there are people who are genuine voters but still excluded, we can extend time for them to submit documents for the purpose of re-entering their names in voter lists.

World.title: A cooling-off period for MPs, MLAs who quit? SC to decide
World.content:
SC agrees to examine whether MPs and MLAs who resign voluntarily should bear by-election costs and face a five-year cooling-off period before contesting again.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a development that could impact politics of shifting loyalties, SC Monday agreed to examine whether an MLA or an MP who contests a by-election caused by their voluntary resignation should be made to bear the entire expenses incurred by Election Commission in conducting the previous poll.Senior advocate Shoeb Alam told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that six persons elected on AIADMK tickets to the Tamil Nadu assembly had resigned in May and June after declaration of results and defected to TVK. Two of them resigned, causing by-elections which they went on to win, this time as TVK candidates.Appearing for petitioner K Suthan, Alam said the court was required to examine whether a person who voluntarily resigned as an MLA or MP should be barred for five years from contesting a state or parliamentary election. SC issued notices to Centre, EC and the six AIADMK MLAs who resigned and defected.The trend of lawmakers crossing over to the party in office and quitting their seats to avoid disqualification has caught on. The petitioner has sought legislative or regulatory measures âto create a mechanism for ensuring financial accountability of elected representatives who prematurely resign from their seats without legally recognised compelling circumstances, including introduction of an âElection Expenditure Securityâ to recover cost of resultant bye-electionsâ.He has requested the court to direct Centre and EC to examine and initiate ânecessary legislative and/or regulatory measures to introduce a statutory disqualification or a reasonable cooling-off period to prevent elected representatives who voluntarily and prematurely resign from contesting subsequent pollsâ. Suthan has suggested a five-year cooling-off period.The petitioner contended that none of the vacancies in the six seats was caused by death, permanent disability, disqualification or other compelling circumstance warranting a bypoll. âPublic shouldnât be made to pay twice for polls to the same constituency because of an individualâs personal or political choice to resign,â he said.Refusing to entertain Suthanâs petition, a Madras HC bench led by CJ S A Dharmadhikari had said, âWe are being asked to design a punitive and financial regime that would operate as a fresh disqualification under Constitution and would curtail statutory right to contest election.In our opinion, the same is a matter of legislative policy, not of judicial direction.ââRight to resign a legislative seat is itself a facet of the constitutional scheme governing membership of a House and cannot be burdened with extra-statutory conditions by judicial order, however sound the underlying concern may be,â the HC had said while refusing the plea to impose a five-year cooling-off period on MPs and MLAs who voluntarily resign from their seats in the House concerned.

World.title: From Andamans to Zanskar, e-Sanjeevani bridges distances, posts 50cr consultations
World.content:
PM Modi outlines key milestones in 139th 'Mann Ki Baat' (file photo)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: High fever and laboured breathing threatened the life of Oho-Tahane, a child from Jarawa tribe of Andaman and Nicobar Islands. With specialist care out of reach, health workers turned to e-Sanjeevani for remote consultation. The doctor diagnosed pneumonia, and timely expert intervention helped the childâs condition improve rapidly.Oho-Tahane, a member of one of Indiaâs most vulnerable tribal groups, is among over 50 crore cases, many in far flung areas, facilitated by the national telemedicine service since its launch in Nov 2019.The serviceâs achievement was highlighted by PM Narendra Modi in his âMann Ki Baatâ address Sunday, as he also cited how e-Sanjeevani enabled a doctor to guide a medical team in treating Kunhi Koya (60) in Kalpeni, Lakshadweep, and helped ensure medical assistance for pregnant Kunjang Dolma in Himalayan region of Zanskar.Developed by C-DAC Mohali under the health ministry, e-Sanjeevani facilitates 2.5-3 lakh daily consultations, offers services in 15 languages and is available across all 36 states and UTs. Women account for 57.1% of the platformâs utilisation, while people aged 46 and above account for 40.1% of consultations. Those aged 60 and above account for 16.2%. The platform has recorded a peak of 6,30,315 consultations in a single day.Modi credited the platformâs reach to dedication of doctors, public trust and the effective use of technology. He highlighted 1.9 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, saying they were bringing healthcare closer to rural communities and evolving into wellness centres for village panchayats. Regular health check-ups were becoming more common in rural areas, he said, with e-Sanjeevani playing an important role.The PM also highlighted advances in brain research, referring to Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT-Madras, which he inaugurated this month. The centre has developed a brain imaging technology platform to create high resolution digital 3D images of human brain. Its mission is to map and study 100 human brains in detail using Param Shakti supercomputer..Modi said the initiative could deepen understanding of the brain, particularly as conditions such as Alzheimerâs disease and dementia lack a definitive cure. Data from the 100 brains will be available as an open-source resource for researchers, the PM added.

World.title: ED in SC: NewsClick received 86cr in ‘illicit foreign funding’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In its appeal before the Supreme Court in the NewsClick case,

(ED) has questioned the news portalâs ownership and service arrangements with foreign entities. The agency has said the Peoples Dispatch website was initially owned and controlled by NewsClick, while the American Justice and Education Fund was paying NewsClick to upload material onto it.

The enforcement agency has questioned the commercial justification for those payments.

ED filed a fresh plea in SC in the case against NewsClick and its â illicit foreign fundingâ with details of NewsClickâs modus operandi, its receipt of nearly Rs 86 crore in foreign funds through arrangements âdesigned to make foreign contributions appear as legitimate business transactionsâ.

According to ED, the issue was not simply that NewsClick had received foreign money.

The issue was that foreign charitable contributions were deliberately presented as investments and commercial payments to circumvent Indian regulations governing foreign funding of news organisations. The agency has cited recovered emails, company documents, financial transactions, valuation reports, contracts and statements recorded during its investigation as evidence.

Agency sources said NewsClick had received payments from US-based Justice and Education Fund (JEF) for articles, videos and other content uploaded onto Peoples Dispatch.





âThe service agreement was a device for regular foreign funding rather than a genuine commercial arrangement,â a senior official said.

âAn email dated Aug 21, 2017, from the portalâs former HR head Amit Chakraborty explicitly discussed changing NewsClickâs company documents to obtain foreign investment without permission from the ministry of information and broadcasting. The email stated: The purpose of the same is that we want foreign investment without the permission of the ministry of information,â according to the agency.

Sources said ED had relied on statement of the portalâs Prashanth Radhakrishnan that JEF owned peoplesdispatch.org only from April 2021 and NewsClick owned it previously. It was NewsClickâs team that determined content quality and terms, supporting its contention that JEFâs payments were not ordinary armâs length purchases.

âThis has acquired wider relevance following recent Fox News reports concerning tech entrepreneur Neville Roy Singham, Tricontinental and their alleged links to international protest movements, including demonstrations in Paris,â an official said.

World.title: OBC candidate scores higher than general aspirant, but didn’t make the cut
World.content:
NEW DELHI: An overage OBC candidate from Tripura became eligible to take the test for recruitment of constables for CAPFs, NIA, Secretariat Security Force and rifleman in Assam Rifles after taking age-relaxation benefit available for reserved category candidates but was not selected despite securing higher marks than a selected general category candidate.

The cut-off mark for OBC candidates was 60, which was higher than that for general category candidates, which the Centre said was because of the limited number of vacancies available in the OBC category. Moreover, once an OBC candidate availed age-relaxation benefit to become eligible, he could not seek migration from reserved category to general category, it said.

This resulted in OBC candidate Jayant Debnath, despite securing 55.1 marks in the 2018 recruitment test, not being selected, while general category candidate Sagar Debnath got selected with 46.26 marks.

The single-judge bench and the division bench of Tripura HC, concurrently, ruled that Jayant needed to be considered for selection as constable.

Appealing against the HC judgements, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati Monday told an SC bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that recruitment rules clearly specified that once a candidate availed age relaxation on the ground that he belonged to a reserved category, he or she would not be permitted to migrate from reserved category to general category.





The bench agreed to examine the correctness of the HC judgement, which had said there was no legal principle prohibiting candidates belonging to reserved categories from claiming unreserved vacancies merely because they had availed benefits applicable to reserved categories.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Centre said, âThe present case concerns a candidate who admittedly availed age relaxation exclusively available to OBC candidates and thereby became eligible to participate in the recruitment process only under the reserved category.â

It stressed that in such cases, migration from reserved to general category was expressly prohibited by the recruitment rules.

âThe impugned judgement would have far-reaching consequences for recruitments conducted by SSC and other recruiting agencies throughout the country. It would enable candidates who have availed reservation-specific concessions to seek migration to unreserved vacancies contrary to recruitment rules, thereby unsettling concluded selections, disturbing category-wise merit determination, prejudicing the rights of unreserved candidates, and generating widespread administrative uncertainty in public recruitment.

â

World.title: Why Indian women work where they 'can', not always where they 'want'
World.content:
Share of women aged 15+ who are working or looking for work

A lot of this work comes and goes with the farming season.

Now count only women who were working or seeking work in the week before the survey . The Gujarat figure drops from 82.1% to 57.7% .

The gap is widest in the villages: 86.5% of rural women in the Gujarat belt are in the job market, against 7.2% in rural Yamunanagar.

In Haryana's Yamunanagar, it is 10 . Only North East Delhi, at 9.8, is lower.

In the six tribal districts of eastern Gujarat, 82 of every 100 women aged 15 and above are working or looking for work. No district in India scores higher.

1Dahod · Narmada · Dang · Tapi · Chhota Udepur · Mahisagar, Gujarat

8 in 10 women here work. But there's a catch

Tushar Tere, Vishal Patadiya & Yagnesh Mehta

Wearing her pink uniform, Anita Tadvi takes her e-rickshaw to the Statue of Unity in Ektanagar every morning. As tourists begin arriving at the world’s tallest statue in Narmada district, the 25-year-old’s day gathers pace. She drives them around the premises as driver and guide, one of many in this tribal Gujarat belt east of Narmada who are reaping the benefits of tourist inflows since Sardar Patel’s iconic statue was inaugurated in 2018.

Anita Tadvi, 25, e-rickshaw driver at the Statue of Unity. “When I learnt about the requirement for e-rickshaw drivers three years ago, I discussed it with my husband and in-laws. They immediately agreed.”

In India’s first district-level periodic labour force survey (PLFS) released in Sept, the Dahod-Narmada-Dang-Tapi-Chhota Udepur-Mahisagar belt recorded the country’s highest female labour force participation rate of 82.1%. The rural rate was even higher, at 86.5%, suggesting village economies are driving the standout number.

Across these districts, women are working because households need two earners, men migrate for work, farms and livestock require family labour, and govt schemes, NGOs and self-help groups have opened up small livelihood routes.

“Statue of Unity has brought many opportunities for women in our district. When I learnt about the requirement for e-rickshaw drivers three years ago, I discussed it with my husband and in-laws. They immediately agreed,” Tadvi said.

She took driving lessons, obtained a licence and joined a group of around 90 women who drive e-rickshaws at the monument.

Self-help groups that teach making everyday products such as soaps, bamboo items, bags and festive decorations have brought more informal jobs. Tourism has poured into this basket.

“Women in the tribal belt are productive and earn more than men. They not only work outside the house but also shoulder responsibilities at home, leaving them with hardly any free time,” said Vadodara-based entrepreneur Swati Bedekar.

Dinesh Patel, a farmer from Mahisagar district, said many women work as farm hands and can be hired from the labour market. “I need farm labourers regularly in my corn fields. I prefer to hire women as they are productive and dedicated. In our district, women easily find farm jobs,” Patel said.

But high participation does not automatically mean secure work.

Madhu Gayakwad, who is from Dang and heads the sociology department at VNS, said employment opportunities for women had increased but remained uneven and there is scope to do more to improve livelihoods. As PLFS shows, tribal Gujarat’s women are working. The next benchmark is to make this income sustainable enough to change their lives.

Close behind the men. Here, 89.8% of men and 82.1% of women are in the job market, a gap of 7.7 points. Only seven districts in India have a gap under 10 points.

World.title: E100 flex-fuel vehicles get regulatory push ahead of launch
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Paving the way for roll out of flex fuel vehicles (FFVs) that can run on up to E100 â nearly 100% pure ethanol or about 93-95% ethanol-blended with petrol â road transport ministry Monday modified changes in Central Motor Vehicles Rules.

This comes barely months before some car manufacturers launch their E100 models.

FFVs with an internal combustion engine can run on petrol, biofuels like ethanol or methanol, or any mixture of both stored in a single fuel tank. E100 fuels are âintended only for vehicles designed and certified to use itâ.

Officials said this is not applicable for other vehicles.âVehicles that use E20 or normal fuel canât use E85 or E100 fuel.

Hence, the notification doesnât require owners of existing vehicles to switch to these fuel categories or modify their vehicles now or in the future,â said a transport ministry official.

TOI has learnt that the change in rules was essential for type approval and registration of FFVs on E100 considering that vehicle manufacturers are ready with their products.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Depending on the vehicleâs design and certification, the range of blending may extend to E85 or E100, a fuel predominantly consisting of ethanol.Flex fuel technology is used in countries such as Brazil and the US.





Ethanol has a lower fossil carbon footprint than conventional petrol and the use of higher ethanol blends can help reduce tailpipe emission of carbon monoxide (CO) and certain hydrocarbons. Greater ethanol use will also reduce dependence on import of crude oil.

While govt notification will enable OEMs to manufacture FFVs, this wonât be enough to push adoption of these vehicles, experts said. This is evident as even after almost seven months of the launch of E85 cars, only 17 such vehicles have been registered.Industry players called reduction in GST on FFVs from 28% to 5% (on par with EVs) to bring down vehicle cost for buyers and compensate for mileage loss, which is about 27% while using E100 fuel.

Besides, they sought a reduction in fuel cost to around Rs 75 a litre.But a bigger problem is availability of E100 given that there are only a handful of pumps, although it can run on other grades of ethanol-blended fuel.

World.title: Bihar MLC polls: RJD MP Sanjay Yadav writes to ECI to ensure transparent counting
World.content:
A day before the counting of votes, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav on Monday (October 26, 2026) wrote to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of the Election Commission of India (ECI) to ensure free, fair and transparent counting of votes for eight seats in the Bihar Legislative Council polls comprising four Graduates’ and four Teachers’ constituencies.

In the four-page letter, Mr. Yadav urged that all ballot papers whose validity or invalidity is disputed should be examined and decided, in accordance with the applicable election rules, before first-preference counting begins. He added that no doubtful ballot paper should be left undecided until a subsequent round or the final result.

He further wrote that reasons for decisions should be recorded, and authorised election agents should be given an opportunity to raise objections as permitted by the rules.

He also said that no counting officer, staff member or election agent should make any additional mark, signature, line, tick, cross or other notation on a ballot paper, except where expressly permitted by the applicable election rules, adding that the original condition and integrity of every ballot paper must be preserved.

Ban on violet pens used for voting

In the letter, Mr. Yadav wrote that pens of the same type as the violet pens used for marking preferences on ballot papers during polling must not, under any circumstances, be available to or possessed by any counting officer, counting staff member or election agent at the counting centre.

“This safeguard is necessary to prevent unauthorised marking or tampering with ballot papers. In the Chandigarh Mayoral Election case of 2024, the Supreme Court examined the issue of unauthorised markings on ballot papers and the process by which votes were declared invalid. Appropriate safeguards must therefore be implemented to preserve the original condition of ballot papers and prevent unauthorised interference during counting,”Mr. Yadav wrote.

The RJD leader pointed out that all counting officials should follow the applicable election rules and prescribed standards uniformly when determining whether ballot papers are valid or invalid, adding that no ballot paper should be rejected arbitrarily or merely on the basis of personal opinion or vague suspicion.

In the letter. Mr Yadav highlighted that voter eligibility and ballot-paper validity are separate matters; where a legally recognised objection or order of a competent authority exists concerning a voter’s eligibility, the relevant records and prescribed legal procedure should be followed. He added that no ballot paper should be rejected solely on the basis of an unverified allegation.

Videography and preservation of records

He also demanded that videography and monitoring be ensured, as permitted by the applicable rules, particularly during scrutiny of doubtful ballot papers, decisions on valid and invalid ballots, and preparation of counting sheets. Mr. Yadav said that all relevant records should be securely preserved for subsequent examination, if required.

Every authorised election agent should be given a reasonable opportunity, in accordance with the applicable rules, to observe the counting process and raise objections regarding doubtful ballot papers or counting irregularities. Objections and decisions should be duly recorded, Mr. Yadav demanded

The number of valid and invalid ballot papers, the relevant stages of counting, including first-preference counting, and the counting sheets should be reconciled and verified in accordance with the applicable rules. Any discrepancy should be resolved through the prescribed procedure before the result is declared.

He also mentioned that all officials and counting staff should be directed to maintain impartiality, transparency and strict compliance with election rules. Mr. Yadav further wrote that any complaint regarding unauthorised interference or counting irregularities should be investigated fairly, and appropriate action should be taken in accordance with the law.

A copy of the letter is also sent to Vinod Singh Gunjiyal, Bihar Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), as the counting of the votes will begin at 8 a.m. on October 27 at eight counting centres.

Later in the day, a six-member RJD delegation also submitted a memorandum to the Bihar CEO with similar demands. The results of Kosi, Tirhut, Patna, Darbhanga (graduate constituencies) and Saran, Tirhut, Patna, Darbhanga (Teachers’ constituencies) will be declared. Polling for eight MLC seats in Bihar was held on October 23, 2026.

World.title: Amid alleged liquor deaths in Madhya Pradesh’s Dewas, police nab 10 for illicit trade
World.content:
Days after locals alleged the death of around 13 people in a month due to consuming spurious liquor, the police in Madhya Pradesh’s Dewas district have arrested 10 people for allegedly selling illicit liquor in the region, officers said on Monday (October 26, 2026).

According to the police, the crackdown was launched based on information from the district hospital about the deaths of two people on October 15 and 18, whose families alleged that they died after consuming liquor. The 10 accused have been booked under Section 34(2) of the Madhya Pradesh Excise Act, 1915.

The crackdown comes days after Ujjain Divisional Commissioner Asheesh Singh formed a five-member special panel to carry out a detailed probe into the alleged deaths in Chandana and Binjana villages. The Dewas district administration, however, had earlier dismissed new reports and Congress claims, denying any deaths related to spurious liquor while saying that the samples of the two deceased who underwent post-mortem examinations have been sent for forensic tests for clarity. It also said that various liquor samples tested following locals’ allegations were not found to contain poisonous contents.

The locals of the two villages have claimed that 13 people have died so far since September 26. M.P. Congress president Jitu Patwai, who visited the affected villages, also alleged that about 35-40 people had damaged their vision due to spurious liquor.

Speaking to The Hindu, Dewas Superintendent of Police (SP) Punit Gehlot said that the family members of the two deceased had alleged that one Vinod Jaiswal is involved in the sale of illicit liquor in the region, after which a search was launched to nab him.

“We tracked him down today [October 26] when he was trying to flee in a car with two of his associates and arrested them,” he said, adding that seven more people were arrested based on information retrieved from them.

The arrested persons include managers and sales executives of various government-licensed liquor shops in the district, the police said in a statement. The police also seized 56 litres of country-made illicit liquor from the accused, which .

Mr. Gehlot also said that FSL test reports of the two deceased were awaited, and samples of liquor seized from the arrested persons will also be sent for testing, and further legal action will be taken based on that.

A senior district administration, however, maintained that it was “not a hooch tragedy” in the region while citing medical records to claim that many of the deceased had died due to other illnesses.

“We are not denying that a few people may have died due to liquor consumption, but the numbers are exaggerated. Family members of some of the deceased, for whom inquest proceedings were initiated, also did not make any such allegations in their initial statements. But an investigation is going on in the matter, and forensic reports will make things clear whether the liquor was spurious or not,” the official said, requesting anonymity.

Meanwhile, Congress MLA and Leader of Opposition in the State Assembly, Umang Singhar, also visited Chandana village on Monday (October 26, 2026) and sought financial aid of ₹25 lakh each for the kin of the deceased from the government. He also announced ₹50,000 for each deceased family from the Congress Legislature Party (CLP).

World.title: Mumbai Police form SIT to probe Jarange’s ₹500 crore claim as Raut writes to Shah seeking ED probe
World.content:
Mumbai Police on Monday (October 26, 2026) announced a three-person SIT to probe the allegations levelled by Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange Patil. He had earlier claimed that the BJP had given ₹500 Crore to Eknath Shinde to hand it over to him to ‘manage’ the Maratha agitation. Meanwhile, Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Raut on Monday (October 25, 2026) wrote to Union Home Minister Amit Shah seeking probe by the Enforcement Directorate into these claims.

The SIT formed by the Mumbai Police consists of three IPS officers and will be led by Additional Police Commissioner Shailesh Balkawade. The two other members include Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 3) Vijaykant Sagar and DCP (Cyber, Crime Branch) Bajrang Bansode. The order to form the SIT has been issued by Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti.

“Mr Manoj Jarange Patil had held a press conference to relay an audio tape in front of the media. This audio tape had references to certain individuals, and to the exchange of a specific amount. It is important to do the forensic examination and technical examination of this audio, along with an impartial and in-depth probe in the issue. Thus, a Special Investigation Team is being formed,” the order issued on Monday (October 26, 2026) stated.

The claim by Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange Patil has stirred Maharashtra’s politics, drawing a wedge between the alliance partners. He has asked for a thorough probe into the matter, seeking accountability from CM Devendra Fadnavis and DCM Eknath Shinde.

Raut’s letter to Amit Shah

The developments took place on a day when Shiv Sena UBT MP Sanjay Raut wrote a letter to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, seeking an ED probe into it. He said everyone needed to know the action taken by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in the matter, unless he himself had given the money. He sought that Mr. Shah should order an immediate probe in the matter.

“To buy out an agitation, the BJP had given ₹500 Crore. Earlier, it used to buy political leaders. If this kind of money is being spent to stop agitations now, and if the BJP leaders themselves claim that ₹500 crore was given to Shrikant Shinde to be handed over to Jarange Patil, then where is that money now? Jarange says he has not received a single penny. This is a case of Hawala. This matter comes under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. One needs to trace the money now,” Mr. Raut said after writing the letter.

He said the former Home Minister of Maharashtra, Anil Deshmukh, was arrested on alleged claims by the then Mumbai Police Commissioner that he was asked to collect ₹100 Crore. “That was only a claim. Here, Jarange Patil has evidence,” he said, asking why the Prime Minister had not yet acted in the matter.

World.title: Bengal BJP bigwigs soften stand on NCPI after Suvendu Adhikari calls on Sudip Banerjee
World.content:
Sparking speculation of a new strategic alignment between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Nationalist Citizen Party of India (NCPI) ahead of municipal polls, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (October 25, 2026) visited the residence of NCPI leader and Kolkata North MP Sudip Bandyopadhyay.

The meeting was described as a courtesy call by the Chief Minister, but the meeting has led to a change in the stance of party bigwigs towards NCPI. While the leaders of NCPI have been making statements that they want to ally with the BJP in the upcoming civic polls, senior leaders of the BJP had ruled out any such possibility.

Union Minister and BJP MP Sukanata Majumdar, who has been appointed the chairperson of the committee overseeing the party’s preparation for civil polls, had earlier said that the party will field candidates on all 209 seats of Kolkata Municipal Corporation. On Monday (October 26, 2026), Mr. Majumdar said that there is always some “permutation and combination in politics”. State’s Minister for Industries and Commerce Tapas Roy who is considered an arch rival of Sudip Banerjee on Monday (October 26, 2026) said that BJP was an all-India described himself as someone who will also abide by the party discipline.

After the defeat of the Trinamool Congress in the West Bengal Assembly polls in 2026, 20 MPs of the party joined the little-known NCPI. NCPI, which has veteran MPs like Sudip Banerjee and Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, claims itself as the second biggest constituent of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) after the BJP.

The new bonhomie between the BJP and NCPI has caused heartburn among many in the BJP, including old-timers like Samik Bhattacharya, the West Bengal BJP president. Responding to questions by journalists on Monday (October 26, 2026), Mr. Bhattacharya said that “it would take us some thinking before holding hands of those believing in Congress ideology as blood of Syama Prasad Mookerjee is on Congress hands”.

Mr. Bhattacharya has often described Trinamool Congress leaders as a product of the Congress ideology. “BJP has always contested alone. I have been associated with the party when the vote percentage of the party was one percent. I never joined another party,” he said.

The State BJP president made the remarks a day after the State Chief Minister gave a certificate to six-time MP, Sudip Banerjee, by saying, “ I do not think that Sudip Babu has tormented any BJP worker,” Mr. Adhikari had said.

It is not only the bonhomie between the BJP and NCPI that has upset the old-timers in the BJP, but also the warmth between the Democratic Trinamool Congress and the saffron party. DTP, led by Ritabrata Banerjee and Arup Roy, has the support of 65 MLAs in the West Bengal Assembly out of the 80 who were elected on the ticket of Trinamool Congress.

Upset with the rapprochement between former Kolkata Mayor and DTP MLA Firhad Hakim and the ruling party, BJP leader Rakesh Singh, who contested and lost to him from the Kolkata Port seat. made a sarcastic comment. “If everyone in Trinamool is good, what is the problem with Mamata Banerjee? She can be inducted in the BJP too,” the BJP leader said.

World.title: Ex-DMK minister Anbil remanded to judicial custody till Nov 6
World.content:
Former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi was on Monday (October 26, 2026) produced before a court in Chennai following his arrest in a corruption case, and he was remanded to judicial custody till November 6.

Anbil Poyyamozhi, held in the graft case involving alleged collection of money from private school managements by promising government recognition and various statutory approvals, was produced before the Special Court for cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act here at 10.10 pm after a medical check-up at a government hospital.

After hearing the arguments of defence lawyers, Wilson and Saravanan, and Public Prosecutor, John Sathyan, Judge L S Sathiyamurthy remanded Poyyamozhi to judicial custody till November 6.

According to police sources, a special team of the Central Crime Brach (CCB), which is investigating allegations that several crores of rupees were collected as ‘party fund’ from various private school managements across Tamil Nadu, arrested Mr. Poyyamozhi who was the State’s School Education Minister between 2021 and 2026.

This is the first arrest of a senior DMK party functionary and former Minister after the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) came to power, sweeping the DMK out of office.

‘Fleeced private schools’

The case arises from a complaint lodged with the Chennai Police Commissioner by C. Elangovan, secretary of the Tamil Nadu Private Schools Federation, levelling serious charges against B.T. Arasakumar, 59, who was accused of having collected large sums of money by running an unregistered association named the ‘Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association’.

The complainant alleged that Mr. Arasakumar, who was later detained under the Goondas Act, had collected money from private school managements by promising to offer services such as obtaining approvals for upgrading schools, gaining permanent recognition, and securing building plan approvals, using his supposed clout in the then-ruling dispensation, the sources said.

The CCB had included Mr. Poyyamozhi as an accused in the case after evidence emerged during the inquiry pointing to his involvement in alleged corruption.

Muthukumar, a close associate of Mr. Poyyamozhi, was allegedly involved in the scam to the tune of about ₹100 crore. “He is absconding and efforts are on to apprehend him at the earliest. We are tracking some clues that might lead to his location,” a police officer said.

Political vendetta, says Stalin

Former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin has strongly condemned Mr. Poyyamozhi’s arrest, terming it an act of “political vendetta.”

In an official statement, Mr. Stalin accused the ruling administration of attempting to divert public attention from governance failures. “By arresting Anbil Mahesh, who has been fully cooperating with the probe into the allegations against him, the ruling government believes it can divert public attention and cover up the deplorable collapse of law and order and rotting administrative breakdown for a few days. Anbil Mahesh will face the allegations against him legally,” Mr. Stalin said.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Media association challenges privacy law in Supreme Court
World.content:
The Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), which has members drawn from across the media spectrum, including those owned by the Ambani and Adani Groups, have challenged the Union government’s privacy law as a violation of journalistic freedom.

A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is scheduled to hear a batch of petitions filed by activists on October 27.

Also read | Supreme Court to examine impact of data protection law on RTI, investigative journalism

The petition filed by the DNPA, which is also listed before the Bench, challenged specific provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025.

The DNPA said the law was completely in contravention with the law laid down by the Supreme Court in its privacy judgment, which held the right inviolable and fundamental to human dignity and life.

“They impermissibly restrict the fundamental right to information and freedom of speech and expression,” the petition said.

The law fails “to provide any exemption in favour of journalistic activity as a distinct class of processing, entitled to constitutional protection under Article 14 and 19(l)(a) of the Constitution of India and threatens the full spectrum of Journalistic activity carried out by journalists, ground reporters, citizens, whistleblowers, RTI activists, and other stakeholders, and strikes at the core of our democratic framework and runs contrary to the basic tenets of the Constitution of India,” the petition said.

It said publishers, editors, reporters and correspondents were, as a consequence of the law, brought within a regime of notice and prior consent, compelled erasure, and verifiable consent.

Section 36 of the DPDP Act, read with Rule 23 and the Seventh Schedule of the DPDP Rules, vested the Central government with an unbridled and standardless authority to requisition any information from any data fiduciary or intermediary, unaccompanied by judicial oversight, any requirement of necessity or proportionality, or notice to the affected data principal.

“Such a power is capable of being turned to the identification and targeting of journalistic sources and is thus constitutionally infirm,” the petition said.

Section 44 (3) of the DPDP Act, by amending Section 8 (1 )(j) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, has placed every category of “personal information” beyond the reach of disclosure.

Further, by amending the Right to Information Act 2005, the DPDP Act has created an absolute bar on the seeking of information relating to public offices.

World.title: A final surge: On Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s triumph in Brazil
World.content:
At one point, it seemed almost impossible for Brazil’s 80-year-old President, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, to turn the tide after finishing second to Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of elections on October 4. In Brazil’s history, no candidate who has finished second in the first round has gone on to win the presidential run-off. Most of the candidates who dropped out after the first round were from the right. Flávio’s Liberal Party cemented its position in both houses of Congress, while right-wing candidates won several provincial elections. But Lula, a former trade unionist and organiser, who lost a finger in an accident as a teenager, was not ready to give up. Lula and his Workers’ Party identified campaign weaknesses, shifted their attention to economic issues, promised growth and welfare, and persuaded more voters to turn out for Sunday’s run-off. Lula won 51.7% of the vote against Flávio’s 48.2%, a greater lead than his victory against Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio’s father, four years ago. Over the weeks, Lula turned the right-wing’s gains in the first round against it, highlighting the threats that a Bolsonaro victory could pose to democracy and civil rights. Flávio’s campaign pledge to free his father — he is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting to overturn Lula’s 2022 victory, and impeach Supreme Court judges — only heightened the concerns of voters outside the right wing, who rallied behind a familiar face.

Lula unleashed a social media campaign to mobilise younger voters. A WhatsApp channel called ‘Lula’s Army’ with 11 million followers spread his message of continuity. He also announced plans to expand a cash payout scheme for the poor, a new debt relief package and entrepreneur-friendly measures. In the northeast, the Workers’ Party’s stronghold, he gained nearly three million votes and made considerable gains in the working-class neighbourhoods of big cities, including São Paulo. A relatively stable economic record, marked by growth and falling unemployment over the past three and a half years, also lent credibility to Lula’s appeal. His victory bucks the recent trend in South America, where Washington-aligned right-wing and conservative forces have gained ground. While Lula offers predictable stability and social and economic inclusiveness, he could also be, as the President of South America’s largest economy, a voice of resistance to Donald Trump’s imperial ambitions. At the same time, Lula will have to work with a right-wing-controlled Congress to advance his agenda. He should seek to build legislative consensus while focusing on addressing the economic challenges of Brazil, which remains one of the most unequal major world economies.

World.title: SHRC calls for checks on private clinics after boy’s death following tonsil surgery in Kannur
World.content:
The Kerala State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) has directed the Health department to ensure that private clinical establishments comply with prescribed standards and to take legal action against those violating the rules. The directive follows the death of a 17-year-old boy after tonsil surgery at a clinic in Kannur in July 2024.

The Commission issued the directive to the Additional Chief Secretary, Health department, asking the authorities to verify the qualifications and registration of doctors and other staff working at such clinics. It also called for guidelines to ensure the quality of medical services and patient safety, along with an effective monitoring mechanism.

The Commission directed the State Police Chief to order a further investigation into the case registered by the Kannur Town police, under the supervision of a Crime Branch officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police. The investigation should comprehensively examine alleged lapses in treatment, allegations of alterations to medical and nursing records, the qualifications and registration of the doctor who performed the surgery, and the registration status of the clinical establishments concerned, the Commission said.

The order followed a complaint filed by P. Shaji, a native of Kannadiparamba and the boy’s father, over the death of his son. The boy died after undergoing tonsil surgery at a clinic in Kannur on July 17, 2024.

An investigation conducted by the Commission’s inquiry wing, headed by its Inspector General, found that the doctor who operated on the boy did not have the legal authorisation to practise in Keralam. The inquiry report also found that neither the clinic where the surgery was performed nor the clinic to which the boy was subsequently admitted had obtained registration as required under the rules.

The Commission noted discrepancies between the reports of inquiries conducted into the incident under the leadership of the district medical officer. It also observed in its order that there had been culpable negligence in the boy’s death.

World.title: Pezeshkian urges 'regional unity' in meeting with Makkah pact countries in Tehran
World.content:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday called for “regional unity” at a meeting in Tehran with representatives of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, which recently signed the Makkah defence pact.

“I hope that the presence of representatives of important and influential Islamic countries at this meeting will help further consolidate regional unity and cohesion,” Pezeshkian said, according to a statement shared on the presidential website, urging Islamic countries to “stand together and adopt a coordinated position”.

“Muslims are brothers to one another and must stand together as a united front against threats and actions targeting Muslim nations,” he stressed.

Condemning Israel’s actions in Gaza and other regional countries, he said: “We must not allow the Israeli regime to assassinate and aggress against any individual or country whenever it desires. I am confident that if Islamic countries stand alongside each other and adopt a coordinated stance, the possibility of such actions repeating will not exist.”

The Iranian president also criticised the United States for claiming “readiness for negotiation and dialogue simultaneously with attacking Iran” during the war.

Pezeshkian stressed the need for translating political understandings into practical actions, stating: “We are determined to tread this path, but achieving this goal requires Islamic countries to reach a common understanding of their objectives, draw a clear vision, and pursue the implementation of agreements with mutual commitment until results are achieved.”

He cautioned against policies of the United States and Israel that were aimed at “creating a rift among Muslim nations”, and called for heightened vigilance.

The Iranian president also called for increased cooperation among regional countries in various fields.

Iran’s IRIB state broadcaster earlier shared a video of the meeting, saying the quadrilateral meeting on “regional security and stability” had begun. The video showed Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi sitting with Iran’s president, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and security chief Mohsen Rezaei.

Earlier in the day, Inter-Services Public Relations had confirmed that CDF Munir was visiting Tehran, but did not share any further details.

The talks also included Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkiye’s intelligence chief, Ibrahim Kalin.

At the start of the meeting, Iran’s state broadcaster reported the meeting was bringing together Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to discuss “regional cooperation, the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its consequences”, among other topics.

State-run PressTV also shared pictures of the meeting.

Following the meeting, Rezaei, head of Supreme National Security Council, told state television, “Very good discussions took place between us.”

“I feel that a new atmosphere is emerging in the region … I sensed a very positive atmosphere in the discussions among the gentlemen.”

Iranian state television reported that the four countries agreed to continue talks after a “first” meeting in Tehran. It said they “agreed to continue discussions to strengthen cooperation… including on regional peace and security”.

Earlier, Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency quoted the deputy secretary of Iran’s top security body, Ali Bagheri Kani, as saying that the visit was part of efforts to implement the idea of endogenous security in West Asia.

Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, said during a media briefing that the meeting with officials from the three countries would cover “most pressing issues threatening our region”, which included Israel’s expansionist policies, developments in Palestine and Lebanon.

He added that the topic of “top priority on the agenda would be consequences of the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its ramifications for the entire region”.

IRNA further quoted him as saying that this meeting could be a prelude to further steps towards shaping “endogenous security — an issue that we have been insisting on for decades”.

“We emphasise that regional security will not be ensured except by relying on the … security considerations of the countries of the region,” he said, adding that events of the last two years, especially the past eight months, had shown that sustainable and reliable security would only be made possible by “building trust and cooperation among the countries in the region”.

Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly had also confirmed the visit in a post on X. Krimly described the visit as “part of the continued efforts by the Makkah Defence Alliance members for de-escalation between parties involved in the ongoing crisis, and promoting dialogue and diplomatic solutions, in support of the mediation efforts carried out by Qatar and Pakistan”.

“The visit underscores the pivotal role of Makkah Defence Alliance members in reinforcing regional security and stability, and working with all countries in the region to achieve that goal,” he added.

The visit comes as attacks by Houthis have spiralled over recent weeks and rhetoric between Washington and Tehran has grown more heated.

Monday’s planned talks would be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the conflict. Under the Makkah pact, signed in August, an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

CDF Munir had visited Iran last week. During the visit, Iranian leaders had conveyed that the US must take the first steps to rebuild trust, and that the acceptance of Tehran’s seven-point proposal could provide a starting point for renewed negotiations.

According to Iran’s ISNA news agency, Baqaei said during the media briefing that the suggestion for the meeting was made during CDF Munir’s visit to Tehran last week. Tehran reviewed the proposal “favourably … and it is scheduled to be held today”, he added.

War has engulfed the Middle East since late February when the US and Israel launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, just as Washington and Tehran were in the middle of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.

An April ceasefire brought an end to the initial phase of intense bombardment but the two sides have continued to vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel.

Iran claims control over the strait and regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross without its authorisation, while the United States has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.

Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal which laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement.

The war has since spread across the region to include fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.54 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Rs2.16
World.content:
The government on Monday increased the price of petrol by Rs1.54 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.16.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs379.25 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.82 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 27 (Tuesday).

On Friday, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association had urged consumers not to resort to panic buying, as excessive purchases could create market distortions.

The same day, senators raised concerns over fuel supply even after Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani said that there were no supply issues.

PPP’s Sherry Rehman questioned petrol availability for December and Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas warned of a bleak situation amid heightening Middle East tensions.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On Sept 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Senate blocks move to withdraw diplomatic passport privileges from state ministers, advisers
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Monday blocked a private member’s bill seeking to withdraw the free-for-all issuance of diplomatic passports to ministers of state, advisers, special assistants and senior bureaucrats and rejected the motion for introduction of the Passports (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

The bill was moved by PTI Senator Faisal Saleem Rahman, chairman of the Senate Standing Committee on Interior, along with senators Samina Mumtaz Zehri and Saifullah Abro.

Declaring his opposition to the bill, State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry said, “You are bringing an amendment to the authority of the cabinet which you have not seen.”

To this, Senator Faisal responded that the bill was about diplomatic passports, which only ministers should have. “There should be no distribution in the issuance of diplomatic passports,“ he observed.

PPP Senator Zamir Hussain Ghumro argued that a minister of state is also a representative of the Parliament.

According to the copy of the bill available with Dawn, it sought to amend the Passports Act 1974 by inserting a new Section 12A for restriction on diplomatic passport entitlement of ministers of state, advisers, special assistants, federal secretaries and director generals.

It provided that no diplomatic passport shall be issued, re-issued or renewed to a minister of state, adviser to the prime minister, special assistant to the prime minister, federal secretaries other than the foreign secretary, or director general, by virtue of holding such office, and any such passport already held shall be surrendered to the prescribed authority within 30 days of commencement of the Act.

The proposed bill clarified that nothing shall prevent such persons from obtaining or retaining an ordinary or official passport where otherwise entitled, and nothing shall affect any independent entitlement arising by virtue of any other office, appointment or diplomatic assignment which lawfully carries such entitlement.

The bill’s statement of objects and reasons noted that the Passports Rules 2021 provide for the issuance of diplomatic passports to various categories of public office holders, including state ministers and functionaries having the status of minister of state.

“A diplomatic passport is a special travel document of the state, and its issuance should primarily correspond to the nature and requirements of diplomatic or state functions rather than operate automatically as a privilege attached to rank or status,” the bill read.

It said the proposed amendment would not restrict official duties or official foreign travel, as a person may continue to obtain an ordinary or official passport where otherwise entitled.

The bill sought only to provide that holding, or having previously held, the office or status of minister of state, adviser, special assistant, federal secretary other than foreign secretary, or director general shall not, by itself, constitute an entitlement to a diplomatic passport.

It argued that the proposed amendment was intended to ensure a clear and reasonable distinction between diplomatic functions and political status and to promote a transparent and purpose-based system for issuance of diplomatic passports.

Heated exchange among allies triggers PPP walkout

The Upper House also witnessed an exchange of hot words between PML-N’s Nasir Butt and PPP’s Sherry Rehman during the passage of the Consumer Protection (Amendment) Bill 2026.

The bill, moved by Senator Zehri of the Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), was passed despite the PML-N-led government’s opposition.

Butt asked who the PPP was supporting, with PPP senators walking out after the episode.
